 where the taxonomy applies, and usage insight.
- [Authentication](/cli/authentication) — how the CLI obtains the token these commands use.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.text: Cloud Commands. Inspect the networking and regions Alethia discovered in a connected cloud account.

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.heading: Cloud Commands
records.text:
The `cloud` group reads the **inventory** Alethia discovered in a connected cloud account — the
networks (VPCs/VNets), subnets, and regions it swept.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `cloud inventory` calls
`/cli/cloud-identities/ /inventory` with your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operates on
the **active organization** — the cloud identity must belong to it.

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.heading: alethia cloud inventory
records.text:
Show the discovered networking + regions for a cloud identity.

alethia cloud inventory 
alethia cloud inventory -o json

 Argument Required Description 
 ---------- ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes The connected cloud identity's id (from `alethia connector` / the console). 

Renders a **Networks** table (network id, name, region, CIDR, default), a **Subnets** table
(subnet id, name, region, AZ, CIDR, public), and a **Regions** line. Add `-o json` for the full
inventory object; `-o csv` emits the networks rows. Prints `No cloud inventory discovered yet.`
when the account hasn't been swept. Backing call: `GET /cli/cloud-identities/ /inventory`.

records.title: Cloud Commands
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Connector Commands](/cli/commands/connector) — connect a cloud account.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.text: Cluster Commands. List provisioned Kubernetes clusters from the CLI.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: Cluster Commands
records.text:
The command is `alethia cluster` (singular) with a `clusters` alias, so both forms work
interchangeably.

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: alethia cluster list
records.text:
List all provisioned Kubernetes clusters.

alethia cluster list

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: or, equivalently:
records.text:
alethia clusters list

Output:

PROJECT CLUSTER VERSION STATUS ARGOCD NODES REGION COST
api-backend (prod) api-backend-production 1.30 ● active exposed 1/3/5 eu-west-1 $210/mo
data-pipeline (stg) data-pipeline-staging 1.29 ● active port-fwd 1/2/3 us-east4 $95/mo

Shows clusters across your projects with:
- Project (with its environment) and cluster name
- Kubernetes version
- Status — the status message is shown inline when a cluster is degraded or failed
- ArgoCD access — `exposed` (a managed-ingress URL exists) or `port-fwd`
- Node count (min/desired/max)
- Region
- Estimated monthly cost

Pass `-o json` for the full records (including each cluster's ArgoCD URL, instance types, and node sizes).

records.title: Cluster Commands
records.heading: Accessing a Cluster
records.text:
After identifying a cluster, configure kubectl using the provider-specific command:

 
 
 aws eks update-kubeconfig --name api-backend-production --region eu-west-1
 kubectl get nodes
 
 
 gcloud container clusters get-credentials data-pipeline-staging --region us-east4
 kubectl get nodes
 
 
 az aks get-credentials --name my-cluster --resource-group my-rg
 kubectl get nodes

records.title: Connector Commands
records.text: Connector Commands. Connect AWS, GCP, Azure, Alibaba and Hetzner cloud accounts to Alethia entirely from the terminal.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connector Commands
records.text:
The `connector` command group connects your cloud accounts to Alethia so the platform can
provision infrastructure into them. It drives the **same connection flow as the web console's
[Connectors](/console/connectors) page**, but end-to-end from the CLI — there is no need to
open a browser for the default flows.

 
Each connection is a **[cloud identity](/concepts/glossary)** — the credential anchor a
[project](/concepts/glossary) links to (`cloud_identity_id`). "Connector" is the catalog of provider
*types*; the record `alethia connector` creates for your account is a cloud identity. A project
points at exactly one. Every cloud-identity query is filtered by provider, so accounts never leak
across providers.
 

Every connection to a cloud that supports it uses **short-lived, keyless credentials** — AWS
cross-account roles, GCP Workload Identity Federation, Azure federated identity, Alibaba RAM
`AssumeRoleWithOIDC`. No access keys or client secrets are created or stored for any of them.

**Hetzner is the single exception, and the exception is the cloud's.** Hetzner Cloud exposes no OIDC
provider and no role-assumption API, so it authenticates with a scoped API token — see
[`alethia

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: How It Works
records.text:
Each `connector` subcommand runs the same three-stage pipeline, verified server-side:

 aws · gcp · azure · alibaba · hetzner] --> B[Init pending cloud identity]
 B --> C[Run provider setup IAM OIDC role · WIF pool · federated cred · RAM OIDC · API token]
 C --> D[Submit captured credentials]
 D --> E[Server-side verify auth + permission probe]
 E --> F{Verdict}
 F --> G[Connected]
 F --> H[Degraded]
 F --> I[Disconnected]
`} />

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Initialize
records.text: The CLI creates (or reuses) a pending cloud identity for the provider.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Run provider setup
records.text:
The CLI drives the provider's own tooling to create the resources Alethia needs (an IAM OIDC provider +
role, a workload identity pool, or an app registration) and captures the resulting credential
material.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Submit & verify
records.text:
The captured credentials are sent to Alethia, which verifies them **instantly, server-side** — an
auth + provisioning-permission probe (no runner). The identity is marked `Connected`, `Degraded`, or
`Disconnected` and is ready to provision into. Existing resources are discovered separately by the
server-side [asset inventory](/console/connectors/health-and-inventory).

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Prerequisites
records.text:
- You must be authenticated: run [`alethia login`](/cli/authentication) first.
- For the **default** flows, the matching provider CLI must be installed and authenticated
 locally:
 - GCP → `gcloud` (used to drive Google Cloud Shell)
 - AWS → `aws`
 - Azure → `az`
 - Alibaba → `aliyun`
 - Hetzner → **none**; it is a token, so there is nothing to install
- The `--manual` flows require **none** of the above — you run a one-liner in the provider's
 browser shell and paste the result back.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Execution Models
records.text:
Provider Default Why 
 ---------- --------- ----- 
 GCP Runs the installer inside your **Google Cloud Shell** (via local `gcloud`) Cloud Shell is already authenticated to your GCP org and has every tool preinstalled 
 AWS Deploys CloudFormation with the **local `aws` CLI** AWS CloudShell is browser-only — there is no remote-exec CLI 
 Azure Runs the setup script with the **local `az` CLI** Azure Cloud Shell is browser-only — there is no remote-exec CLI 
 Alibaba Runs the setup script with the **local `aliyun` CLI** Alibaba Cloud Shell is browser-only — there is no remote-exec CLI (as with AWS and Azure) 
 Hetzner Prompts for a scoped **API token** Hetzner Cloud has no OIDC or role assumption, so there is nothing to set up — only a credential to capture 

The four keyless providers support `--manual`, which prints a link + command to run in the browser
shell and prompts you to paste the result — use it when you cannot or prefer not to install the local
CLI. Alibaba additionally supports `--terraform`, which writes an OpenTofu module you apply yourself
(see [`alethia connector alibaba`](#alethia-connector-alibaba)).

Hetzner needs no such flow: there is no installer, only the token i

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector gcp
records.text:
Connect a Google Cloud project using Workload Identity Federation.

alethia connector gcp --project my-gcp-project

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project` No GCP project ID. Prompted interactively if omitted. 
 `--manual` No Run the installer in the browser Cloud Shell and paste the result instead of using local `gcloud`. 

By default, the CLI runs an installer **inside your Google Cloud Shell**. Cloud Shell is
authenticated as you, so the provisioner service account and a workload identity pool that trusts
Alethia are created directly in your project — and the CLI captures the generated WIF credential
config automatically. No service account keys are ever created.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Enter the project
records.text: Provide `--project`, or type it at the prompt.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Cloud Shell setup
records.text:
The CLI invokes `gcloud cloud-shell ssh`, pushes the installer, and runs it. The first run can take
a minute while Cloud Shell provisions.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connection test
records.text:
The captured WIF config is submitted, verified instantly server-side, and the identity is marked Connected (or Degraded/Disconnected).

 

Sample run:

◆ Project ── ◇ Cloud Shell setup ── ◇ Connection test

Running installer via gcloud Cloud Shell (the first run can take a minute)...
✔ Cloud Shell ready.
✔ Installer running in Cloud Shell.
...
--- START CONFIG (copy everything below until END CONFIG) ---
{ ...WIF credential config... }
--- END CONFIG ---

✓ Verifying connection (server-side)...
✓ Connected

✓ GCP project "my-gcp-project" connected

 
If `gcloud` is not logged in, Cloud Shell cannot authenticate non-interactively and you will see a
reauth error. Run `gcloud auth login`, then retry — or use `alethia connector gcp --manual`.

✗ gcloud is not authenticated
Run this, then retry:

 gcloud auth login

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Manual GCP setup
records.text:
With `--manual`, the CLI prints a Cloud Shell link and a command, then waits for you to paste the
WIF config:

alethia connector gcp --project my-gcp-project --manual

1. Open [Google Cloud Shell](https://shell.cloud.google.com/cloudshell/open?shellonly=true&show=terminal).
2. Run the printed command:
 curl -sO https://alethia-connector-assets.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/alethia-gcp-setup.sh \
 && bash alethia-gcp-setup.sh my-gcp-project
 3. Paste everything between `--- START CONFIG ---` and `--- END CONFIG ---` at the prompt.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector aws
records.text:
Connect an AWS account using a keyless, issuer-direct IAM role (an IAM OIDC provider trusting the Alethia
issuer — no access keys, no external id).

alethia connector aws

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--region` No AWS region for the CloudFormation stack. 
 `--role-name` No Name for the IAM role. Defaults to `AlethiaProvisionerRole`. 
 `--manual` No Deploy from the AWS console and paste the role ARN instead of using local `aws`. 
 `--script` No Use the `aws`-CLI setup script instead of the CloudFormation stack. 

 
 

The CLI deploys the bundled CloudFormation template with your local `aws` credentials, then reads
the created role ARN from the stack outputs and submits it automatically.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Initialize
records.text: Alethia creates a pending cloud identity for the connection.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Create the IAM role
records.text:
The CLI runs `aws cloudformation deploy` (stack `AlethiaConnect`), creating an IAM OIDC provider for the
Alethia issuer + a role that trusts it via `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` (pinned to the fixed audience and
subject).

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connection test
records.text:
The role ARN is submitted, the connection is verified instantly server-side, and the identity is marked Connected (or Degraded/Disconnected).

 

alethia connector aws --region eu-west-1

 
 

With `--manual`, the CLI prints a CloudFormation **quick-create** link pre-filled with the Alethia issuer
URL and prompts for the resulting role ARN:

alethia connector aws --manual

1. Open the printed quick-create link (it pre-fills the template and issuer URL).
2. Acknowledge the IAM capabilities checkbox and create the stack.
3. Copy the `RoleArn` from the stack **Outputs** tab and paste it at the prompt:
 ? Role ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AlethiaProvisionerRole

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector azure
records.text:
Connect an Azure subscription using federated identity (no client secret).

alethia connector azure --subscription 

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--subscription` No Azure subscription ID. Prompted interactively if omitted. 
 `--manual` No Run setup in Azure Cloud Shell and paste the result instead of using local `az`. 

 
 

The CLI runs the setup script with your local `az` login. It creates a user-assigned managed
identity (a plain ARM resource — no app registration, no client secret), a federated credential
trusting Alethia's OIDC issuer, and a least-privilege role assignment, then captures the tenant,
client, and subscription IDs automatically.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Enter the subscription
records.text: Provide `--subscription`, or type it at the prompt.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Create the managed identity
records.text:
The CLI runs the setup script via `az`, creating the managed identity, federated credential, and
role assignment.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connection test
records.text:
The captured IDs are submitted, the connection is verified instantly server-side, and the identity is marked Connected (or Degraded/Disconnected).

 

 
 

With `--manual`, the CLI prints a command to run in Azure Cloud Shell and prompts for the three
IDs the script outputs:

alethia connector azure --subscription --manual

1. Open [Azure Cloud Shell](https://shell.azure.com).
2. Run the printed command:
 curl -sO https://alethia-connector-assets.s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/alethia-azure-setup.sh \
 && bash alethia-azure-setup.sh 
 3. Paste the **Tenant ID**, **Client ID**, and **Subscription ID** it prints at the prompts.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector alibaba
records.text:
Connect an Alibaba Cloud account using keyless `AssumeRoleWithOIDC`. By default the CLI runs a setup
script with your local `aliyun` CLI: it creates a RAM OIDC provider trusting the Alethia issuer plus
a RAM role, and captures the resulting role ARN automatically. Use `--manual` to run the same script
in the Alibaba Cloud Shell, or `--terraform` to apply an OpenTofu module instead. Alethia stores
nothing but the role ARN — no AccessKey.

alethia connector alibaba

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--region` No Alibaba region for the RAM provider. Defaults to `cn-hangzhou`. 
 `--manual` No Run the setup script in the Alibaba Cloud Shell and paste the role ARN. 
 `--terraform` No Apply the OpenTofu module instead of running the setup script. 
 `--dir` No Directory to write the OpenTofu module into (with `--terraform`). Defaults to `./alethia-alibaba-connector`.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Initialize
records.text: Alethia creates a pending [cloud identity](/concepts/glossary) for the connection.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Create the RAM role
records.text:
The CLI runs the setup script with your local `aliyun` CLI, creating a RAM OIDC provider trusting the
Alethia issuer (` /api/oidc`) plus a RAM role, and captures the role ARN from its
output. With `--manual`, run the same script in the Alibaba Cloud Shell and paste the ARN back.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Connection test
records.text:
The role ARN is submitted, verified instantly server-side, and the identity is marked Connected (or
Degraded/Disconnected). Alethia stores nothing but the role ARN — no AccessKey.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: OpenTofu module (--terraform)
records.text:
With `--terraform`, the CLI writes `main.tf` into the target directory (`--dir`) instead of running
the setup script. It provisions the same RAM OIDC provider + role. Authenticate to Alibaba (the
`aliyun` CLI, or `ALICLOUD_ACCESS_KEY` / `ALICLOUD_SECRET_KEY`), apply it, then paste the `role_arn`
output at the prompt:

cd alethia-alibaba-connector
tofu init
tofu apply -var "region=cn-hangzhou" -var "alethia_issuer_url=https://alethialabs.io/api/oidc"

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector hetzner
records.text:
Connect a Hetzner Cloud account with a scoped API token.

bash

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Prompted, masked — the token never reaches your shell history
records.text: alethia connector hetzner

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: From a pipe, for scripts and CI
records.text: echo "$HCLOUD_TOKEN" alethia connector hetzner --token-stdin

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: With Object Storage credentials, if this project declares storage buckets
records.text:
alethia connector hetzner --token-stdin \
 --s3-access-key "$HETZNER_S3_ACCESS_KEY" --s3-secret-key "$HETZNER_S3_SECRET_KEY"

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--token-stdin` No Read the API token from stdin. Preferred for scripts. 
 `--token` No Pass the token inline. Convenient, but it lands in your shell history and the process list. 
 `--s3-access-key` No Hetzner Object Storage access key. Only needed for storage buckets. 
 `--s3-secret-key` No Hetzner Object Storage secret key. 

Create the token in the Hetzner Cloud Console, under the **project** rather than the account:
**Security → API tokens → Generate API token**, with **Read & Write**. Object Storage uses a
separate pair under **Security → S3 credentials**.

federation — an AWS cross-account role, GCP Workload Identity Federation, an Azure federated
credential, Alibaba RAM `AssumeRoleWithOIDC` — so Alethia stores no secret at all. Hetzner Cloud
exposes neither an OIDC provider nor a role-assumption API, so a token is the only mechanism it
offers. The limit is Hetzner's, not Alethia's. The toke

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector list
records.text:
List all connected (verified) cloud accounts.

alethia connector list

Output:

PROVIDER ACCOUNT CONNECTED
AWS AWS (123456789012) 2 hours ago
GCP GCP (my-gcp-project) 5 days ago
AZURE Azure (3f9a1c2b-...) 5 days ago

The table is interactive — sort and navigate with the keyboard (see [TUI Components](/cli/tui)).

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: alethia connector remove
records.text:
Disconnect a cloud account.

alethia connector remove gcp

If you omit the provider, the CLI shows a picker of connected accounts.

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `-y`, `--yes` No Skip the confirmation prompt. 

 
Disconnecting resets the identity to a pending state and **orphans any projects** that referenced it
(their `cloud_identity_id` is cleared). It does not destroy already-provisioned cloud resources —
run [`alethia project destroy`](/cli/commands/plan-and-apply) first to tear those down. You can
reconnect the same provider later.

records.title: Connector Commands
records.heading: Troubleshooting
records.text:
Symptom Cause & fix 
 --------- ------------- 
 `gcloud is not authenticated` / reauth error Cloud Shell cannot prompt non-interactively. Run `gcloud auth login`, then retry — or use `--manual`. 
 `gcloud CLI not found on PATH` Install the [Google Cloud CLI](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install), or use `--manual`. 
 `aws CLI not found on PATH` / `az CLI not found on PATH` Install the provider CLI, or use `--manual` to set the connection up from the browser. 
 `could not find WIF config in installer output` The Cloud Shell installer did not finish. Re-run, or use `--manual` and paste the config yourself. 
 `Captured WIF config is not valid JSON` The pasted block was truncated. Copy everything between `--- START CONFIG ---` and `--- END CONFIG ---`. 
 Connection test fails Alethia could not assume the credentials. Confirm the role trust policy pins the Alethia issuer + sub/aud (AWS), the workload identity binding (GCP), or the federated credential + least-privilege role (Azure). The verify runs inline server-side and returns the reason with the result — re-run the connector command to see it. 
 `Invalid format. Expected: arn:aws:iam::…` The pasted role ARN is malformed — copy t

records.title: Cost Commands
records.text: Cost Commands. Inspect a project environment's infrastructure cost — the latest Infracost breakdown a plan captured.

records.title: Cost Commands
records.heading: Cost Commands
records.text:
The `cost` group reads a project environment's **infrastructure cost**. Every PLAN runs Infracost
over the terraform plan and records the priced breakdown per environment; this command shows the
latest one.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `cost show` calls `/cli/projects/ /cost` with
your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operates on the **active organization**
(`alethia org switch`, or `--org ` per invocation).

records.title: Cost Commands
records.heading: alethia cost show
records.text:
Show the latest cost for a project environment.

alethia cost show --project my-project
alethia cost show -p my-project -e staging
alethia cost show -p my-project -o json

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project`, `-p` Yes Project name or id. 
 `--env`, `-e` No Environment name, stage, or id. Omit to use the project's default environment. 

The command prints a one-line headline — the total monthly cost, or **not priced** when no plan has
ever costed the environment (an honest "we don't know yet", never a fabricated zero) — followed by a
table of the priced resources:

Cost [staging]: $123.45/mo USD (captured 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z)
Address Type Monthly
aws_db_instance.main aws_db_instance $100.00
aws_s3_bucket.logs aws_s3_bucket $23.45

Add `-o json` for the full cost object (`priced`, `total_monthly`, `currency`, `captured_at`,
`plan_job_id`, `environment`, `resources[]`); `-o csv` emits the priced-resource rows. Backing call:
`GET /cli/projects/ /cost?env= `.

records.title: Drift Commands
records.text: Drift Commands. Inspect a project's day-2 drift posture — which managed resources have diverged from their provisioned state.

records.title: Drift Commands
records.heading: Drift Commands
records.text:
The `drift` group reads the **day-2 drift posture** of a project — the "keep proving it" half of
Alethia. A `DETECT_DRIFT` job runs a refresh-only plan and records which managed resources have
diverged from their provisioned state; this command shows the latest result.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `drift show` calls `/cli/projects/ /drift`
with your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operates on the **active organization**
(`alethia org switch`, or `--org ` per invocation).

records.title: Drift Commands
records.heading: alethia drift show
records.text:
Show the latest drift posture for a project, optionally scoped to one environment.

alethia drift show --project my-project
alethia drift show -p my-project -e production
alethia drift show -p my-project -o json

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project`, `-p` Yes Project name or id. 
 `--env`, `-e` No Environment name, stage, or id. Omit to use the latest posture across the project. 

The command prints a one-line headline — **in sync**, **N resource(s) drifted**, or **not
evaluated** when no drift scan has ever run (an honest "not proven", never a false in-sync) —
followed by a table of the drifted resources:

Drift [production]: 2 resource(s) drifted (scanned 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z)
Address Type Change
aws_db_instance.main aws_db_instance modified
aws_s3_bucket.logs aws_s3_bucket deleted

Add `-o json` for the full posture object (`evaluated`, `in_sync`, `drifted`, `scanned_at`,
`environment`, `details[]`); `-o csv` emits the drifted-resource rows. Backing call:
`GET /cli/projects/ /drift?env= `.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.text: IaC Commands. Inspect the BYO Terraform/OpenTofu source attached to a project environment.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: IaC Commands
records.text:
The `iac` group shows the **BYO Terraform/OpenTofu source** attached to an environment — your own
IaC module, pulled from a connected git repo, that Alethia applies for that environment.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `iac show` calls `/cli/projects/ /byo-iac`
with your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operates on the **active organization**.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: alethia iac show
records.text:
Show the BYO IaC source attached to a project environment.

alethia iac show --project my-project
alethia iac show -p my-project -e staging
alethia iac show -p my-project -o json

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project`, `-p` Yes Project name or id. 
 `--env`, `-e` No Environment name, stage, or id. Omit to use the project's default environment. 

Renders a field/value card: **name**, **repo**, **path**, **ref**, **enabled**, **scan** (the
IaC-safety scan lifecycle), **pinned commit** (what a deploy will apply), **deployed commit** (what
the last deploy applied), **status**. Prints `No BYO IaC source attached.` when none is configured.
Add `-o json` for the full source object (the elench scan report itself is console-only). Backing
call: `GET /cli/projects/ /byo-iac`.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: alethia iac attach
records.text:
Attach a git repository holding your own Terraform/OpenTofu to one environment.

alethia iac attach -p shop -e dev \
 --repo https://github.com/acme/infra --path iac/drift/aws --ref main \
 --var region=eu-west-1

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--repo` Yes Git repository URL. 
 `--path` No Path to the module within the repo. 
 `--ref` No Git ref (branch, tag or SHA). 
 `--var key=value` No A scalar tfvar. Repeatable. 
 `--git-credential-id` No Credential for a private repository. 

An environment holds **at most one** source, so re-attaching replaces it.

 
 `--var` takes **scalars only** — string, number or bool. The server refuses a nested object or an
 array, and tfvars are never a place for a secret. Use the platform's secret handling for anything
 sensitive.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: alethia iac scan
records.text:
alethia iac scan -p shop -e dev

An attached source is **not deployable until scanned**: the scan reads the module's variables and
records the verdict the plan-time gate reads. The printed job id follows with
`alethia jobs logs --follow`.

records.title: IaC Commands
records.heading: alethia iac detach
records.text:
alethia iac detach -p shop -e dev --yes

 
 Detaching stops Alethia managing what the source created. Resources it applied are **not
 destroyed** — run a destroy first if that is what you want.
 

 
 These commands need `ALETHIA_BYO_IAC_ENABLED=true` on the instance, and attaching is refused with
 **409** when the environment already holds template-provisioned state — a conflict with reality that
 no retry will clear.

records.title: Command Reference
records.text: Command Reference. Complete reference for all alethia CLI commands organized by group.

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: Command Reference
records.text:
alethia organizes its commands into groups (`connector`, `project`, `runner`, `jobs`, `cluster`,
`org`, `members`, `teams`, `channels`, `alerts`, `roles`, `grants`, `sso`, `fleet`,
`classification`, `ops`), a set of read-only inspection groups (`repo`, `cloud`, `agent`, `addon`,
`chart`, `iac`, `cost`, `drift`, `verify`, `probes`), plus top-level auth (`login`/`logout`/`init`), identity
(`whoami`/`config`/`open`), `billing`, `usage`, `activity`, and utility commands. All commands
communicate with the Alethia [Console](/concepts/glossary) API — they never run
[OpenTofu](/concepts/glossary) (the `tofu` binary) locally. Provisioning (`tofu plan`/`apply`/
`destroy`) happens on a [Runner](/runner); the CLI only queues and observes it.

Every command also accepts the [global flags](/cli/identity#output-formats) `-o, --output ` and `--no-input`.

records.title: Command Reference
records.heading: Command Tree
records.text:
alethia
├── init # first-run: pick control-plane URL, then log in
├── login [-f/--force] [--web-origin ]
├── logout
├── whoami # current user, active org, role, plan, default runner
├── config # show resolved config + file paths + web-origin source
│ ├── set # key: web-origin
│ ├── get [web-origin active-org]
│ ├── clear-context # clear the active org
│ └── export [project] [--format ] [--out ] # export a project's resolved config
├── version
├── open [console docs] # aliases: docs, dashboard
├── completion [bash zsh fish powershell]
├── org # aliases: orgs
│ ├── list
│ └── switch [org]
├── members # alias: member
│ ├── list
│ ├── add [--role member]
│ └── remove 
├── teams # alias: team
│ ├── list
│ ├── create 
│ └── delete 
├── connector # manage cloud identities (credential anchors)
│ ├── gcp [--project ] [--manual]
│ ├── aws [--region ] [--role-name ] [--manual]
│ ├── azure [--subscription ] [--manual]
│ ├── alibaba [--region ] [--dir ]
│ ├── list
│ └── remove [provider] [-y/--yes]
├── project
│ ├── list
│ ├── get [--open]
│ ├── create --region [--cloud-identity-id ] [--stage ] [--iac-version ]
│ ├── env # manage a project's environments (--project )
│ │ ├── list
│ │ └── add [-

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.text: First-Run Setup (init). One command to point the CLI at a control plane and log in — the hosted default, or a self-hosted / dev URL.

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: First-Run Setup
records.text:
`alethia init` is the guided one-time setup: it picks the **control-plane URL**, persists it, then
runs the browser [device-code login](/cli/authentication). It's exactly the composition of
[`alethia config set web-origin`](/cli/commands) + [`alethia login`](/cli/authentication) in a single
prompt — nothing more.

alethia init

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Choose the control-plane URL
records.text:
A form asks for the **control-plane URL**, pre-filled with the current value — the hosted
`alethialabs.io` by default, or your self-hosted / dev origin. The entered value is validated
(must be `http`/`https` with a host) and saved with the trailing slash stripped.

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Log in
records.text:
The device-code flow runs immediately: the CLI opens ` /cli/login?device_code= ` in your
browser and polls ` /api/auth/cli/exchange` until you approve, then writes the tokens. See
[Authentication](/cli/authentication) for the full RFC 8628 flow.

 

 
**On the hosted platform you can skip `init` entirely** — the default origin already points at
`alethialabs.io`, so `alethia login` on its own is enough. Reach for `init` (or set `web-origin`
directly) when you run a **self-hosted** console or a **local dev** stack.

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: How the control-plane URL resolves
records.text:
The CLI resolves the origin in this precedence — highest first:

 B[persisted config web-origin]
 B --> C[hosted default alethialabs.io]
`} />

- **`ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN`** — an environment variable, wins for the current shell. Handy for CI or a
 throwaway override without touching the config file.
- **Persisted `web-origin`** — what `alethia init`, `alethia config set web-origin `, and
 `alethia login --web-origin ` write. Stored in the on-disk CLI config.
- **Hosted default** — the built-in `alethialabs.io` origin, used when neither of the above is set.

`alethia config` shows the resolved origin **and its source** (`env` / `config` / `default`), plus
the on-disk config and credentials paths:

alethia config
alethia config get web-origin # just the resolved origin

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Equivalent one-shots
records.text:
`init` is convenience glue. Any of these do the same job piecemeal:

bash

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Set the origin once, then log in
records.text:
alethia config set web-origin https://alethia.internal.example.com
alethia login

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Or set-and-log-in in a single command (persists the origin, then runs the device flow)
records.text: alethia login --web-origin https://alethia.internal.example.com

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Per-shell override without persisting (e.g. dev / CI)
records.text:
alethia login

 
`init`'s **URL prompt** honors `--no-input`: with prompting disabled it takes the already-resolved
origin without asking. The **login** step still needs a browser to approve the device code — for a
fully non-interactive machine, provision credentials another way (`ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN` + a
pre-seeded credentials file). See [Configuration](/cli/configuration).

records.title: First-Run Setup (init)
records.heading: Where things are stored
records.text:
`init` writes to the standard per-user config directory (`os.UserConfigDir()/alethia/`): the
control-plane URL and active-org context to the CLI config file, and the login tokens to a separate
credentials file. `alethia config` prints both exact paths. See
[Configuration](/cli/configuration) for the file formats and
[Authentication](/cli/authentication) for token lifetimes and refresh.
