records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Authentication](/cli/authentication) — the device-code flow, token refresh, `logout`.
- [Configuration](/cli/configuration) — config keys, env vars, file locations.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree.

records.title: Job Commands
records.text: Job Commands. List, stream logs, and cancel infrastructure jobs.

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: Job Commands
records.text:
Monitor and manage provision jobs from the terminal. For how jobs work internally, see [Job Queue Pattern](/concepts/job-queue).

 
There is no `alethia jobs wait` command. To block until a job finishes, pass `-w/--wait` to the
command that queues it — `project plan apply destroy` and `runner deploy destroy`. See
[Plan & Apply](/cli/commands/plan-and-apply).

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: alethia jobs list
records.text:
List jobs for the active organization.

alethia jobs list [--status ] [-n/--limit ]

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--status` No Filter by status: `QUEUED`, `CLAIMED`, `PROCESSING`, `SUCCESS`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`. 
 `-n`, `--limit` No Jobs per page (default `20`). 

Output:

TYPE STATUS PROJECT RUNNER CREATED DURATION
Plan SUCCESS api-backend fleet-hcloud-1 2 min ago 1m 12s
Deploy PROCESSING api-backend fleet-hcloud-1 30 sec ago 28s…
Destroy QUEUED data-platform — just now —

The **TYPE** column is one of the full job-type set the Runner executes — not just the three above:

 Type What the Runner does 
 ------ ---------------------- 
 `PLAN` `tofu plan` + the [verify](/concepts/glossary) gate over the plan JSON — no mutation. 
 `DEPLOY` `tofu plan` → verify gate → `tofu apply` → ArgoCD scaffold. 
 `DESTROY` `tofu destroy` — tears the project's infrastructure down. 
 `DEPLOY_RUNNER` / `UPDATE_RUNNER` / `DESTROY_RUNNER` Provision, upgrade, or tear down a self-deployed Runner. 
 `ANALYZE_REPO` Inspect a connected git repository (repo-onboarding analysis). 
 `DETECT_DRIFT` `tofu plan -refresh-only` → a per-environment drift posture. 
 `AUDIT` Re-run t

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: alethia jobs get
records.text:
Get detailed information about a specific job. The job ID is a **positional argument**.

alethia jobs get 

Shows: type, status, assigned Runner, all timestamps, the elench `verify_result` summary on PLAN/DEPLOY jobs, and the error message (if failed). Add `-o json` for the full execution metadata (OpenTofu outputs, cost data).

The `Verify` line here is a one-line summary — a verdict and a count. To check the receipt's
signature, see what it is sealed to, or read the per-control report behind that verdict, use
[`alethia verify receipt`](/cli/commands/verify) and `alethia verify show`.

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: alethia jobs logs
records.text:
Stream job logs to the terminal. The job ID is a **positional argument**.

alethia jobs logs [-f/--follow]

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes Job ID (positional) 
 `-f`, `--follow` No Continuously stream new log entries (like `tail -f`) 

Without `--follow`, prints all existing logs and exits. With `--follow`, the command blocks and prints new log lines as the Runner writes them. Logs include `tofu` (OpenTofu) plan/apply output, resource creation progress, and error messages.

Press `Ctrl+C` to stop following.

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: alethia jobs cancel
records.text:
Cancel a queued or in-progress job. The job ID is a **positional argument**.

alethia jobs cancel 

Sets the job status to CANCELLED. If the job is currently being executed by a Runner, the Runner detects the cancellation on its next status check and terminates the `tofu` process gracefully.

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: Waiting for jobs
records.text:
To block on a job from a script, queue it with `-w/--wait` rather than polling:

bash

records.title: Job Commands
records.heading: Plan and block until it finishes, then apply and block again
records.text:
alethia project plan --project-id $ID --wait
alethia project apply --project-id $ID --plan-job-id $PLAN_JOB --wait

See [Plan & Apply](/cli/commands/plan-and-apply) for the full workflow.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.text: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity). Manage notification channels and alert rules, and read the delivery/activity log, from the alethia CLI.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: Notifications
records.text:
Alethia's notification system has three parts, all manageable from the CLI:

- **Notification channels** are delivery destinations — webhook, email, Slack, PagerDuty, and more —
 that alert rules fan out to.
- **Alert rules** bind product events (event-key patterns) to one or more channels.
- The **activity log** is a durable record of every action, denial, and alert delivery.

All commands operate on the **active organization** (set via `alethia org switch`); override
per-invocation with `--org `. Every command accepts the global
[`-o, --output `](/cli/identity#output-formats) flag.

 
Alerts require a **Pro plan or higher**. Channel secrets (webhook/Slack URLs, PagerDuty routing
keys) are encrypted at rest and never returned by the API — the CLI only shows whether a secret is
configured.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia channels
records.text: Alias: `channel`.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: channels list
records.text:
Lists the active organization's notification channels. On a TTY this opens the interactive table;
with `--output json csv` (or `--no-input`) it prints a static table.

alethia channels list
alethia channels list -o json

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: channels create
records.text:
Creates a channel. The destination depends on `--type`; the endpoint is **verified before the
channel is saved** (a channel never exists unverified).

 Type Required destination flag(s) 
 ---------------------------- ----------------------------------- 
 `email` one or more `--recipient ` 
 `slack` / `webhook` / others `--url ` (+ `--signing-secret`) 
 `pagerduty` `--routing-key ` 

bash

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: Slack/webhook
records.text: alethia channels create "Ops Slack" --type slack --url https://hooks.slack.com/services/XXX

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: Email (repeat --recipient for multiple)
records.text: alethia channels create "On-call" --type email --recipient sre@example.com --recipient lead@example.com

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: PagerDuty
records.text: alethia channels create "PD" --type pagerduty --routing-key R0UT1NGKEY

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: channels verify <id>
records.text:
Sends a synthetic test event through the channel and marks it verified.

alethia channels verify 3f1c…

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: channels delete <id>

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia alerts
records.text:
Alias: `alert`. An alert rule binds one or more **event-key patterns** (e.g. `system.job.failed`,
`authz.*.denied`) to notification channels.

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alerts list
records.text:
Lists the active organization's alert rules with their bound channel count.

alethia alerts list
alethia alerts list -o json

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alerts create
records.text:
Creates a rule. Repeat `--event` and `--channel` for multiple values.

alethia alerts create "Job failures" \
 --event system.job.failed \
 --channel 3f1c… \
 --severity critical

 Flag Description 
 ------------ ---------------------------------------------------- 
 `--event` Event-key pattern (repeatable, required) 
 `--channel` Channel id to route to (repeatable, required) 
 `--severity` `info`, `warning` (default), or `critical`

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alerts delete <id>
records.text:
Deletes an alert rule (prompts for confirmation). Matching events will no longer be routed.

alethia alerts delete a1b2…

records.title: Notifications (Alerts, Channels & Activity)
records.heading: alethia activity
records.text:
Reads the active organization's delivery/activity log — every recorded action and denial, newest
first, including alert deliveries.

alethia activity # latest 50
alethia activity -n 200 # latest 200
alethia activity -o json

 Flag Description 
 --------------- -------------------------------------------- 
 `-n, --limit` Maximum number of entries to show (default 50)

records.title: Ops Commands
records.text: Ops Commands. Break-glass incident-recovery verbs — audited, reason-gated, cross-tenant actions for on-call operators.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: Ops Commands
records.text:
The `ops` group is the terminal-first **break-glass** surface: privileged incident-recovery
actions for on-call operators. Every verb hits the same audited `/api/breakglass/*` endpoints as
the operator UI, with the same bearer [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and the same append-only
audit trail.

 
The entire surface is gated behind the `ALETHIA_BREAKGLASS_ENABLED` flag **and** the
`BREAKGLASS_OPERATORS` server-side allowlist. A non-operator — or a deployment that has not enabled
break-glass — is refused with a 403/404. Membership in an organization is **not** the wall: these
endpoints are cross-tenant and bypass row-level security, so the operator allowlist is the only gate.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: The break-glass model
records.text:
Three rules hold for every action, enforced server-side:

- **Audited.** An append-only audit record is written *before* the act. Every verb requires
 `--reason`, which is recorded in the immutable audit.
- **Typed-confirm.** A mutating action must echo the exact resource id back to the server; a
 mismatch is refused. The CLI sends this confirmation for you.
- **Two-person approval for high-blast actions.** `force-release-lock`, `state-surgery`, and
 `orphan-clean` require an `--approval` token minted by a **different** operator via
 [`alethia ops approve`](#alethia-ops-approve). The server enforces that the approver and the actor
 are different people.

Each action opens a fresh time-boxed break-glass session before it runs, records the reason, then
executes against the single audited execute endpoint.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: Blast radius
records.text:
Each verb is labelled with its blast radius in its help text.

 Blast Verbs 
 ------- ------- 
 none (read-only) `inspect-job`, `orphan-detect` 
 low `retry-job`, `cancel-job`, `drain-runner`, `replay-webhook` 
 medium `unstick-env`, `restart-runner` 
 HIGH (two-person) `force-release-lock`, `state-surgery`, `orphan-clean`

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops session
records.text:
Open a standalone time-boxed break-glass session. The action verbs open their own session; this is
for inspecting or warming a session, or for scripts that reuse one.

alethia ops session --reason "incident-1234 triage"

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--reason` Yes Reason recorded in the immutable audit. 

Prints the session id, the resolved operator, and the session's expiry.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops approve
records.text:
Mint a single-use, TTL'd, two-person approval bound to a high-blast action and resource. Run this as
the **second** operator; the acting operator then passes the printed id as `--approval`.

alethia ops approve --reason "incident-1234 sign-off"

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes The action to approve: `force_release_state_lock`, `state_surgery`, or `orphan_clean`. 
 ` ` Yes The resource the approval is bound to. 
 `--reason` Yes Reason recorded in the immutable audit. 

Prints the approval id, its expiry, and a note.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops inspect-job
records.text:
Read a job's full row cross-tenant. Read-only (blast: none).

alethia ops inspect-job --reason "why did DEPLOY hang"

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes Job id (positional). 
 `--reason` Yes Reason recorded in the immutable audit.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops retry-job
records.text:
Re-enqueue a fresh job from a stuck or failed one (blast: low).

alethia ops retry-job --reason "runner crash, safe to retry"

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops cancel-job
records.text:
Cancel a job and signal its Runner to stop mid-flight (blast: low).

alethia ops cancel-job --reason "wrong project targeted"

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops unstick-env
records.text:
Move a stuck environment to a target status through the `set_env_status` compare-and-swap primitive —
never a raw `UPDATE` (blast: medium). You must pass the explicit expected-from set and the target; a
CAS miss is refused.

alethia ops unstick-env \
 --from PROVISIONING,DEPLOYING --to READY \
 --reason "stuck after runner crash"

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes Environment id (positional). 
 `--from` Yes Comma-separated expected current statuses (the CAS precondition). 
 `--to` Yes Target status to move the environment to. 
 `--reason` Yes Reason recorded in the immutable audit.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops drain-runner
records.text:
Mark an online Runner `DRAINING` so it stops claiming jobs (blast: low).

alethia ops drain-runner --reason "node degraded"

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops restart-runner
records.text:
Drain a Runner and wake the scaler to roll a replacement (blast: medium).

alethia ops restart-runner --reason "wedged runner"

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops force-release-lock
records.text:
Force-release a stranded [OpenTofu](/concepts/glossary) state lock (blast: HIGH, two-person). It
rotates the fencing token and bumps the generation — never a naive delete — so a zombie writer is
fenced out.

alethia ops force-release-lock \
 --approval \
 --reason "runner died holding the lock"

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes State key of the locked object (positional). 
 `--approval` Yes Two-person approval token id (mint one with `alethia ops approve`). 
 `--reason` Yes Reason recorded in the immutable audit.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops state-surgery
records.text:
Queue a privileged `STATE_SURGERY` job through the normal Runner/state pipeline, with fencing intact
(blast: HIGH, two-person).

alethia ops state-surgery \
 --approval \
 --note "import orphaned RDS instance" \
 --reason "failed apply orphaned a resource"

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes State key to operate on (positional). 
 `--approval` Yes Two-person approval token id. 
 `--note` No Free-form description of the intended repair (audit only). 
 `--reason` Yes Reason recorded in the immutable audit. 

 
The runner-side executor ships **inert** (fail-closed): the queued job fails cleanly without
mutating state. See the `STATE_SURGERY` job type in [Job Commands](/cli/commands/jobs).

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops orphan-detect
records.text:
List orphan candidates for a single project. Read-only and run-scoped — never account-wide
(blast: none).

alethia ops orphan-detect --project --reason "post-incident sweep"

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project` Yes Project id to scope the scan to. 
 `--reason` Yes Reason recorded in the immutable audit.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops orphan-clean
records.text:
Force-destroy detected orphans across clouds (blast: HIGH, two-person) — the most dangerous action.

alethia ops orphan-clean \
 --project \
 --approval \
 --reason "cleanup approved"

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project` Yes Project id to scope the clean to. 
 `--approval` Yes Two-person approval token id. 
 `--reason` Yes Reason recorded in the immutable audit. 

 
`orphan-clean` ships **inert**. It refuses unless the deployment is separately armed with
`ALETHIA_BREAKGLASS_ORPHAN_CLEAN_ENABLED`, and even when armed it is unimplemented rather than
performing an unscoped delete.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: alethia ops replay-webhook
records.text:
Re-dispatch a stored Stripe webhook event through the same idempotent handler the live webhook uses
(blast: low).

alethia ops replay-webhook --reason "missed invoice.paid"

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes Stripe event id (positional). 
 `--send-emails` No Re-send the branded emails on replay. Suppressed by default — the emails are the one non-idempotent side effect. 
 `--reason` Yes Reason recorded in the immutable audit.

records.title: Ops Commands
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Job Commands](/cli/commands/jobs) — the `STATE_SURGERY` job type and the job lifecycle.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.text: Organizations, Members & Teams. Switch the active organization and manage its members and teams from the CLI.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.text:
alethia scopes everything you do — projects, runners, jobs, connectors — to an **active
organization**. The active org is persisted locally (in `~/.config/alethia/config.json`) and sent as
the `X-Alethia-Org` header on every request.

The `members` and `teams` commands operate on the active org by default; pass `--org ` to target
a different one for a single invocation.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia org
records.text: Manage the organizations you belong to. Aliases: `orgs`, `organization`, `organizations`.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia org list
records.text:
List the organizations you belong to. The active org is marked in the `Active` column.

alethia org list

Output:

NAME SLUG ROLE PLAN ACTIVE
Acme acme owner pro ◆
Personal you owner free

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia org switch
records.text:
Set the active organization. Pass an org **id, slug, or name**; with no argument, pick one
interactively.

bash

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: Explicit
records.text: alethia org switch acme

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: Interactive picker (TTY only)
records.text:
alethia org switch

The selection is persisted locally and sent as `X-Alethia-Org` on subsequent commands. Clear it with
[`alethia config clear-context`](/cli/configuration#alethia-config).

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia org settings
records.text:
Show the active organization's general settings.

alethia org settings
alethia org settings -o json

Renders a field/value card: **name**, **slug**, **description**, **region** (the org's default
provisioning region), **default env**, and **terraform** (the default OpenTofu version). Prints
`Not in an organization (community mode).` when the caller has no real org (personal scope). Backing
call: `GET /cli/org-settings`.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia members
records.text:
Manage members of the active organization. Alias: `member`.

 Command Description 
 --------- ------------- 
 `alethia members list` List members of the active org. 
 `alethia members add [--role member]` Invite a member by email. `--role` defaults to `member`. 
 `alethia members remove ` Remove a member by id. 

alethia members list
alethia members add teammate@example.com --role member
alethia members remove mbr_123

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: Target a specific org instead of the active one
records.text:
alethia members list --org org_456

 Flag Description 
 ------ ------------- 
 `--org ` Operate on this org instead of the active one. 
 `--role ` (`members add` only) Role for the invited member. Default `member`.

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: alethia teams
records.text:
Manage teams within the active organization. Alias: `team`.

 Command Description 
 --------- ------------- 
 `alethia teams list` List teams (name + member count). 
 `alethia teams create ` Create a team. 
 `alethia teams delete ` Delete a team by id. 

alethia teams list
alethia teams create platform
alethia teams delete team_123

records.title: Organizations, Members & Teams
records.heading: Target a specific org
records.text:
alethia teams list --org org_456

 Flag Description 
 ------ ------------- 
 `--org ` Operate on this org instead of the active one. 

 
All of these commands honor the global `-o, --output ` flag — e.g.
`alethia members list -o json jq`. See [Identity & Global Options](/cli/identity).

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.text: Plan & Apply. Queue plan, deploy, and destroy jobs from the CLI.

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: Plan & Apply
records.text:
These `project` subcommands queue infrastructure operations that [Runners](/runner) execute. They
implement the Plan-Review-Apply workflow from the terminal.

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: alethia project plan
records.text:
Queue an [OpenTofu](/concepts/glossary) plan job — the Runner runs `tofu plan`.

alethia project plan [--project-id ] [--runner-id ] [--wait]

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project-id` No Project UUID (interactive selector if omitted) 
 `--runner-id` No Specific Runner to execute (any available if omitted) 
 `--wait` No Block until the job completes 

On success, prints the job ID. Use `alethia jobs logs --follow` to stream the plan output.

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: alethia project apply
records.text:
Queue a deployment (apply) job.

alethia project apply [--project-id ] [--runner-id ] [--plan-job-id ] [--wait]

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project-id` No Project UUID (interactive selector if omitted) 
 `--runner-id` No Specific Runner to execute 
 `--plan-job-id` No Reference a specific plan to apply 
 `--wait` No Block until the job completes 

The `--plan-job-id` flag ensures the apply uses the exact plan you reviewed. If the Project configuration changed since the plan was generated, the job fails with a [config hash mismatch](/console/jobs/plan-and-apply).

 
A DEPLOY job is `tofu plan` → **[verify](/concepts/glossary) gate** → `tofu apply` → ArgoCD scaffold.
The verify gate is **fail-closed**: a hard control failure blocks *before* `tofu apply` unless an
authorized override waives it. The report is attached to the job's `execution_metadata` and rendered
in the console Plan tab — inspect it with `alethia jobs logs --follow`.

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: alethia project destroy
records.text:
Destroy a Project's provisioned infrastructure.

alethia project destroy [--project-id ] [--runner-id ] [--wait]

Queues a DESTROY job. The Runner runs `tofu destroy` to tear down all resources. OpenTofu state is preserved (it lives behind the Console state proxy, not on the Runner), so accidental destroys can be recovered by re-applying.

 
To tear down a deployed **Runner** (not a Project), use [`alethia runner destroy`](/cli/commands/runners).

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: Interactive Selection
records.text:
When `--project-id` is omitted, alethia launches a TUI selector:

1. Select a Project from the list
2. The command proceeds with the selected Project

See [TUI Components](/cli/tui) for details on the interactive selectors.

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: Scripting Examples
records.text: bash

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: Plan and wait, then apply
records.text:
JOB_ID=$(alethia project plan --project-id $PROJECT_ID --wait 2>&1 grep "Job ID" awk '{print $3}')
alethia project apply --project-id $PROJECT_ID --plan-job-id $JOB_ID --wait

records.title: Plan & Apply
records.heading: Destroy with wait
records.text: alethia project destroy --project-id $PROJECT_ID --wait

records.title: Probe Commands
records.text: Probe Commands. Inspect a project's cluster-alive probes — the "is it still up?" day-2 signal per environment.

records.title: Probe Commands
records.heading: Probe Commands
records.text:
The `probes` group (alias `probe`) lists the latest **cluster-alive probe** per environment — the
"is it still up?" half of day-2, alongside [drift](/cli/commands/drift)'s "has it diverged?". A
`PROBE_CLUSTER` job dials each environment's cluster API server; this shows the most recent result.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `probes list` calls `/cli/projects/ /probes`
with your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operates on the **active organization**
(`alethia org switch`, or `--org ` per invocation).

records.title: Probe Commands
records.heading: alethia probes list
records.text:
List a project's latest per-environment cluster probes.

alethia probes list --project my-project
alethia probes list -p my-project -o json

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project`, `-p` Yes Project name or id. 

Columns: **Environment**, **Reachable** (`● up`, `○ down`, or `— never probed`), **Message** (why
unreachable, when down), **Probed** (when the last probe ran). Every environment is listed; one
that has never been probed shows `never probed` rather than being hidden.

Environment Reachable Message Probed
production ● up — 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
staging ○ down dial tcp: timeout 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
dev — never probed — —

Add `-o json` for the raw probe objects; `-o csv` for the rows. Backing call:
`GET /cli/projects/ /probes`.

records.title: Probe Commands
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Drift Commands](/cli/commands/drift) — the divergence half of day-2.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Project Commands
records.text: Project Commands. List and inspect infrastructure configurations from the CLI.

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Project Commands
records.text:
Projects are infrastructure configurations (an *app* that owns one or more environments). The CLI
can both **read** projects (`list`, `get`) and **author** them — create a project, manage its
environments, and CRUD its component resources — so the whole project lifecycle is scriptable.

All authoring commands operate on the **active organization** (set via `alethia org switch`, or
`--org`). Every command accepts the global `-o, --output ` flag.

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: alethia project list
records.text:
List all Projects.

alethia project list

Output:

ID PROJECT PROVIDER REGION ENV STATUS
a1b2... api-backend aws eu-west-1 production ACTIVE
c3d4... data-pipeline gcp us-east4 staging DRAFT

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: alethia project get
records.text:
Get detailed information about a specific Project. The project is identified by a **positional
project name** (not a flag).

alethia project get api-backend

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes Project name (positional) 
 `--open` No Open the project in the web console. (Long-only — `-o` is the global `--output` flag.) 

Shows the full Project configuration including:
- Project name, provider, region, environment
- Status and estimated monthly cost
- Component summary (network, cluster, databases, caches, etc.)
- Cloud identity reference

When run interactively without `--open`, the CLI offers to open the project in the browser after
printing it.

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: alethia project create
records.text:
Create a new project in the active organization. A default environment is created with it; add
component resources afterwards with `alethia project component add`.

alethia project create api-backend --region eu-west-1 --cloud-identity-id 

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes Project name (positional) 
 `--region` Yes* Cloud region to provision into (*prompted on a TTY when omitted) 
 `--cloud-identity-id` No Cloud account to link (interactive picker on a TTY when omitted) 
 `--stage` No Initial environment stage: `development` (default), `staging`, `production` 
 `--iac-version` No OpenTofu version to pin (defaults server-side) 
 `--placement-mode` No Placement of the default environment: `namespace`, `vcluster`, `dedicated` (default) 
 `--env` No `name:stage[:mode[:namespace]]`, repeatable — the full environment matrix 

The created project prints as a card (or the typed object with `--output json`).

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Creating the whole environment matrix at once
records.text:
`--env` declares every environment and **how each is placed onto a Fabric**, in one command. The
first entry is the default environment and owns the Fabric it provisions, so it defaults to
`dedicated`; later entries default to `namespace` and share that Fabric.

alethia project create shop --region eu-west-1 --cloud-identity-id \
 --env prod:production \
 --env dev:development:namespace:boutique-dev \
 --env staging:staging:vcluster

That is **one** cluster hosting three environments. Omit `--env` and you get the default
Production + Preview pair instead.

 
 Placement is the flag with a bill attached. Each `dedicated` environment is a separate cluster with
 its own OpenTofu state; `namespace` and `vcluster` share the Fabric that already exists. A four-cloud
 two-tier demo is four clusters with placement and eight without it.

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: alethia project env
records.text:
A project owns N independently-provisionable environments. The project is named with `--project`
(its name **or** id).

bash

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: List a project's environments
records.text: alethia project env list --project api-backend

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Add an environment (shares the existing Fabric by default)
records.text: alethia project env add staging --project api-backend --stage staging

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Add one as a vcluster on a named Fabric, with its own destination namespace
records.text:
alethia project env add staging --project shop --stage staging \
 --placement-mode vcluster --fabric shared --namespace boutique-staging

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Add one that provisions its OWN cluster
records.text:
alethia project env add prod --project shop --stage production --placement-mode dedicated

 Command Flags Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `env list` `--project ` List the project's environments (default first) 
 `env add ` `--project ` `--stage ` `--region ` `--placement-mode ` `--fabric ` `--namespace ` `--lifecycle ` Add an environment (name is slugified; region inherits the project's when omitted) 

An **added** environment defaults to `namespace` placement on the Fabric the project's default
environment already uses — the cheap rung, and the one that makes a second tier free. `--fabric`
names a different Fabric to place onto; `--namespace` sets the ArgoCD destination namespace
(otherwise derived from the environment name); `--lifecycle` is `persistent` (default) or
`ephemeral`. `--fabric` and `--namespace` are ignored for `dedicated`, which owns a new Fabric.

The success line names the placement you got, so a `dedicated` you did not intend is visible
immediately rather than on the next apply.

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: alethia project component
records.text:
One uniform group authors **all** of a project's component resources. The project is named with
`--project`, and the environment with `--env`.

Supported **kinds** — singletons (one per project *per environment*, name-less): `network`,
`cluster`, `dns`, `observability`, `repositories`; and multi (named, many per environment):
`databases`, `caches`, `queues`, `topics`, `nosql_tables`, `container_registries`, `secrets`,
`storage_buckets`.

bash

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: List the supported kinds
records.text: alethia project component kinds

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: List a project's components (optionally filter by --kind and/or --env)
records.text: alethia project component list --project api-backend --kind databases

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Add a database (multi kind → --name required)
records.text:
alethia project component add --project api-backend --kind databases --name main \
 --set engine=postgres --set port=5432 --set iam_auth=true

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Configure the cluster singleton (--name ignored; upserts)
records.text:
alethia project component add --project api-backend --kind cluster \
 --set cluster_version=1.31 --set node_min_size=2 --set 'instance_types=["t3.medium"]'

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Remove components (destructive → confirms)
records.text:
alethia project component remove --project api-backend --kind databases --name main
alethia project component remove --project api-backend --kind network

 Command Flags Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `component kinds` — List the supported component kinds + their cardinality 
 `component list` `--project ` `--kind ` `--env ` List components (all kinds, or one) 
 `component add` `--project ` `--kind ` `--name ` `--env ` `--set key=value`… Create a component 
 `component remove` `--project ` `--kind ` `--name ` `--env ` Delete a component (confirms)

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Components belong to an environment
records.text:
A component is scoped to one **environment**, not to the project as a whole — so two environments
can hold the same kind with different configuration. `--env` takes an environment id, name or stage:

bash

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: dev and staging deploy DIFFERENT overlays of the same repo
records.text:
alethia project component add --project shop --env dev --kind repositories \
 --set apps_destination_repo=https://github.com/acme/shop --set apps_path=overlays/dev

alethia project component add --project shop --env staging --kind repositories \
 --set apps_destination_repo=https://github.com/acme/shop --set apps_path=overlays/staging

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: Inspect one tier at a time
records.text:
alethia project component list --project shop --env staging

What `--env` defaults to differs by verb, deliberately:

- **`add` and `remove`** default to the project's **default environment**, so a single-environment
 script needs no `--env` at all.
- **`list`** defaults to **every** environment. Narrowing a read silently would hide rows you did
 not ask to hide.

 
 `remove` deletes from **one** environment — the one you named, or the default. It never touches a
 sibling environment's copy. Confirm the tier in the success line (`Component removed in staging`)
 before assuming which one went.

records.title: Project Commands
records.heading: The --set field setter
records.text:
`--set key=value` is repeatable and generic. Each value is parsed as JSON when it can be, else taken
literally — so numbers, booleans, and arrays are typed correctly:

--set port=5432 # number
--set iam_auth=true # boolean
--set instance_types='["t3.medium"]' # array
--set engine=postgres # string

Fields are **validated server-side** against the component's schema: an unknown or mistyped field
fails with a clear `400`, naming the offending field and the allowed set. Singleton kinds ignore
`--name` (they upsert the project's single row); multi kinds require it.

records.title: Promotion Commands
records.text: Promotion Commands. Inspect environment promotions — status, approval tally, and approval slots.

records.title: Promotion Commands
records.heading: Promotion Commands
records.text:
The `promotion` group (aliases `promotions`, `promo`) reads a project's **environment promotions** —
moving a source environment's proven design into a target environment, gated by that environment's
[protection rules](/cli/commands/protection).

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. These subcommands call
`/cli/projects/ /promotions[/…]` with your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operate on
the **active organization**. Approving, rejecting, or cancelling a promotion stays in the console.

records.title: Promotion Commands
records.heading: alethia promotion list
records.text:
List a project's promotions, newest first.

alethia promotion list --project my-project
alethia promotion list -p my-project -e production # filter by target environment
alethia promotion list -p my-project -o json

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project`, `-p` Yes Project name or id. 
 `--env`, `-e` No Filter to promotions targeting this environment (name, stage, or id). 

Columns: **ID**, **Source**, **Target**, **Status**, **Created**. Backing call:
`GET /cli/projects/ /promotions`.

records.title: Promotion Commands
records.heading: alethia promotion get
records.text:
Show one promotion's status, approval tally, and approval slots.

alethia promotion get --project my-project

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ----------------- ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes The promotion id (from `promotion list`). 
 `--project`, `-p` Yes Project name or id. 

Renders a summary card (source → target, status, **approvals** `N/M`, initiator, created, any
error) followed by the approval slots (status, approver, required role, decided-at). The per-gate
evaluation detail and full config diff stay in the console. Add `-o json` for the full object.
Backing call: `GET /cli/projects/ /promotions/ `.

records.title: Promotion Commands
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Protection Commands](/cli/commands/protection) — the gates a promotion must pass.
- [Staged Commands](/cli/commands/staged) — an environment's pending canvas changes.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Protection Commands
records.text: Protection Commands. Inspect a project's promotion protection rules — the gates that guard deploys into each environment.

records.title: Protection Commands
records.heading: Protection Commands
records.text:
The `protection` group (alias `protect`) lists the **promotion protection rules** configured per
environment: the gates that must pass before a promotion deploys into that environment.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `protection list` calls
`/cli/projects/ /protection` with your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operates on the
**active organization** (`alethia org switch`, or `--org ` per invocation).

records.title: Protection Commands
records.heading: alethia protection list
records.text:
List a project's per-environment protection rules.

alethia protection list --project my-project
alethia protection list -p my-project -o json

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project`, `-p` Yes Project name or id. 

Columns: **Environment**, **Predecessor** (predecessor stage must be deployed + in-sync),
**Verify** (elench verify must pass), **Approval** (a human must approve), **Approvers** (minimum
approver count), **Soak (min)** (minutes since the predecessor deploy), **Cost Δ** (a plan cost
delta above this USD/mo flips the promotion to pending-approval). A configured gate renders as a
check; an unset gate or limit renders as `—`. Only environments with rules configured appear.

Environment Predecessor Verify Approval Approvers Soak (min) Cost Δ
production ✓ ✓ ✓ 2 30 $100.00
staging — ✓ — — — —

Add `-o json` for the raw rule objects; `-o csv` for the rows. Backing call:
`GET /cli/projects/ /protection`.

records.title: Protection Commands
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Drift Commands](/cli/commands/drift) · [Cost Commands](/cli/commands/cost) — the posture the
 verify/cost gates act on.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Provider Commands
records.text: Provider Commands. Inspect and re-verify connected cloud provider identities from the terminal.

records.title: Provider Commands
records.heading: Provider Commands
records.text:
The `provider` group (alias `providers`) reads and re-verifies an existing **cloud provider
connection**. Use [`alethia connector`](/cli/commands/connector) to create or change a connection;
these commands only inspect and re-probe one.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. These subcommands call `/cli/providers/ /*`
with your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operate on the **active organization**
(`alethia org switch`, or `--org ` per invocation).

records.title: Provider Commands
records.heading: alethia provider status
records.text:
Show the connection status of a cloud provider identity.

alethia provider status aws
alethia provider status gcp -o json

 Argument Required Description 
 ---------- ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `alibaba`, or `hetzner`. 

Renders a field/value card: **status** (`connected` `disconnected`), the **identity** id, and the
provider-specific identity fields that are set (AWS account id / role arn, GCP project id / service
account, Azure tenant / client / subscription). Add `-o json` for the raw `ProviderStatus`.

Backing call: `GET /cli/providers/ /status`.

records.title: Provider Commands
records.heading: alethia provider verify
records.text:
Re-run the server-side health probe (auth + provisioning-capability check) against the connected
identity for a provider. The server verifies **inline** — there is no job to poll.

alethia provider verify aws

 Argument Required Description 
 ---------- ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `alibaba`, or `hetzner`. 

The command resolves the connected identity via `status`, then re-verifies it and renders the
verdict: **identity**, **status**, **verified**, and — when degraded — the **missing permissions**.
It exits non-zero when there is no connected identity to verify or the probe reports the identity is
not connected, so it is safe to use in a script or CI gate.

Field Value
identity id-1
status connected
verified true

Backing call: `POST /cli/providers/ /verify` with `{ identity_id }`.

records.title: Provider Commands
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Connector Commands](/cli/commands/connector) — connect or change a cloud provider account.
- [Identity](/cli/identity) — how connections and keyless credentials work.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Repository Commands
records.text: Repository Commands. Browse the git repositories Alethia can see through a connected git provider.

records.title: Repository Commands
records.heading: Repository Commands
records.text:
The `repo` group (aliases `repos`, `repositories`) lists the repositories reachable through a
connected **git provider** — GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket. These are the repositories you can point
a project at when authoring its infrastructure.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API — it authors nothing locally. `repo list` calls
`/cli/repositories/ ` with your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and the git connection on
your **active organization** (`alethia org switch`, or `--org ` per invocation).

records.title: Repository Commands
records.heading: alethia repo list
records.text:
List repositories for a connected git provider.

alethia repo list # defaults to --provider github
alethia repo list --provider gitlab
alethia repo list --provider bitbucket -o json

 Flag Default Description 
 ------ --------- ------------- 
 `--provider` `github` Git provider to list from (`github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`). 

Columns: **Name** (the repo's full `owner/name`, falling back to its short name), **Visibility**
(`public` `private`), **Default branch**, **URL**. In an interactive TTY this renders as a
navigable [TUI table](/cli/tui); otherwise it prints a plain table. Add `-o json` for the raw
`Repository` objects (id, name, full_name, url, private, default_branch, provider).

Name Visibility Default branch URL
acme/app private main https://github.com/acme/app
acme/site public trunk https://github.com/acme/site

Backing call: `GET /cli/repositories/ `.

records.title: Repository Commands
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Connector Commands](/cli/commands/connector) — connect a cloud provider account.
- [Authentication](/cli/authentication) — how the CLI obtains the token these commands use.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Runner Commands
records.text: Runner Commands. Deploy, list, and tear down runner agents from the CLI.

records.title: Runner Commands
records.heading: Runner Commands
records.text: Runners execute infrastructure jobs. Manage them with `alethia runner`.

records.title: Runner Commands
records.heading: alethia runner deploy
records.text:
Deploy a new runner to an AWS account. Creates a runner record and queues a
`DEPLOY_RUNNER` job using the latest stable release.

alethia runner deploy --cloud-identity-id --name --region 

 Flag Description 
 ------ ------------- 
 `--cloud-identity-id` Cloud identity to deploy into (AWS only) 
 `--name` Runner name 
 `--region` Cloud region 
 `--assigned-runner-id` Which runner executes the deployment 
 `--wait`, `-w` Wait for job completion 

 
 **Deployed runners are available on AWS only.** `infra/templates/runner/` holds one template,
 `aws`, so there is no runner template for GCP, Azure, Alibaba Cloud or Hetzner. Omit
 `--cloud-identity-id` and the picker lists your verified AWS accounts alone. Pass an identity
 for another cloud and the server refuses the deploy before it creates a runner or a job.

 This limits **where the runner itself runs**, not what it provisions: a registered runner
 provisions every cloud Alethia supports, wherever it runs. To run a runner on another cloud, use
 [`alethia runner register`](#alethia-runner-register) — see also
 [self-operated runners](/runner/self-hosted).

records.title: Runner Commands
records.heading: alethia runner register
records.text:
Register a runner you operate yourself. Nothing is provisioned — this is the command for every cloud
`runner deploy` cannot reach.

alethia runner register my-hetzner-box

records.title: Runner Commands
records.heading: Bound to a cloud account, and machine-readable for a provisioning script
records.text:
alethia runner register gcp-box-1 --cloud-identity-id 

 Argument / Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 ` ` Yes* Runner name (positional, or `--name`) 
 `--cloud-identity-id` No Bind the runner to a cloud account 

It prints the two values the runner process needs, as assignments you can paste straight into an env
file or a systemd unit:

✓ Registered runner my-hetzner-box (7f3c…)

ALETHIA_RUNNER_ID=7f3c…
ALETHIA_RUNNER_TOKEN=9a1b…

 
 **The token is shown once.** Only its SHA-256 is stored, so it cannot be re-read or recovered — a
 leak of the runners table yields nothing usable, and a token you lose is a runner you re-register.
 Copy it before the terminal scrolls.
 

Then start the runner with those two variables set and confirm it appears in
`alethia runner list` with a recent heartbeat. See
[self-hosted runners](/runner/self-hosted) for the process itself.

records.title: Runner Commands
records.heading: alethia runner list
records.text:
List all runners (status, operator, version, last heartbeat). The **Operator** column shows `managed` or, for self runners, `self · deployed` / `self · registered`.

alethia runner list

records.title: Runner Commands
records.heading: alethia runner destroy
records.text:
Tear down a runner's cloud infrastructure. Queues a `DESTROY_RUNNER` job; another
runner executes the teardown.

alethia runner destroy --runner-id 

 Flag Description 
 ------ ------------- 
 `--runner-id` ID of the runner to destroy 
 `--assigned-runner-id` Which runner executes the teardown 
 `--wait`, `-w` Wait for job completion

records.title: Runner Commands
records.heading: alethia runner remove
records.text:
Remove a runner's database record only (no cloud teardown). Run
`alethia runner destroy` first to tear down cloud resources.

alethia runner remove

records.title: Staged Change Commands
records.text: Staged Change Commands. Inspect an environment's staged (pending) canvas changes — the diff an apply would push.

records.title: Staged Change Commands
records.heading: Staged Change Commands
records.text:
The `staged` group reads an environment's **staged (pending) canvas changes** — the durable diff
between the edited canvas and the environment's live config, i.e. the Pending Changes an apply would
push.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. `staged list` calls `/cli/projects/ /staged`
with your [CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operates on the **active organization**. Staging,
discarding, or applying changes stays in the console/canvas.

records.title: Staged Change Commands
records.heading: alethia staged list
records.text:
List an environment's staged changes.

alethia staged list --project my-project
alethia staged list -p my-project -e staging
alethia staged list -p my-project -o json

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--project`, `-p` Yes Project name or id. 
 `--env`, `-e` No Environment name, stage, or id. Omit to use the project's default environment. 

Columns: **Op** (`create` `update` `delete`), **Component** (the canvas node kind), **Component
ID** (the target row for update/delete; `—` for create), **Created**. The per-change payload delta
stays console-only. Prints `No staged changes.` when the environment is in sync. Backing call:
`GET /cli/projects/ /staged`.

records.text:
- [Promotion Commands](/cli/commands/promotions) — moving a proven design between environments.
- [Command Reference](/cli/commands) — the full command tree and global flags.

records.title: Verify Commands
records.text: Verify Commands. Pull a job's signed evidence receipt, check its ed25519 signature against a key your control plane vouches for, and read the per-control report.

records.title: Verify Commands
records.heading: Verify Commands
records.text:
Every `PLAN` and `DEPLOY` job carries an **elench evidence receipt**: the per-control verification
report, sealed to the hash of the exact OpenTofu plan that was applied, and signed with ed25519.
The `verify` group reads that receipt from the terminal.

`alethia verify receipt` checks the signature and **exits non-zero when it cannot**, so you can gate
a deployment pipeline on it. `alethia verify show` prints the report behind the verdict.

 
The CLI is a client of the same Console API. Both commands call `/cli/jobs/ ` with your
[CLI token](/cli/authentication) and operate on the **active organization**
(`alethia org switch`).

records.title: Verify Commands
records.heading: alethia verify receipt
records.text:
Fetch a job's receipt and verify it.

alethia verify receipt --job 4f3c2b1a-...
alethia verify receipt -j 4f3c2b1a-... -o json
alethia verify receipt -j 4f3c2b1a-... --key-file alethia-receipts.pub

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--job`, `-j` Yes Job id. `alethia jobs list` prints them. 
 `--key` No Verify against this base64 ed25519 public key instead of the trusted set. 
 `--key-file` No Same, read from a file. 
 `--allow-unsigned` No Exit zero when the receipt carries no signature. 
 `--allow-untrusted` No Exit zero when the signature is self-consistent but its key is not vouched for. 

alethia · verify receipt
 Signature ✓ signature verified against your organization's own recorded key
 Trust org
 Algorithm ed25519
 Key ID 9f2c4a1b7e5d3068
 Verdict pass
 Sealed to plan 3b1f...c204
 Control catalog elench-controls-0.5.2
 Controls 14 pass, 0 fail, 0 warn, 0 n/a

records.title: Verify Commands
records.heading: What a green check means
records.text:
The signature is verified against a key **the control plane vouches for** — your organization's own
recorded signing key, or the Alethia platform key — fetched from `GET /cli/signing-keys`.

This matters more than it looks. A receipt carries the public key it was signed with, so it will
always verify against *itself*, whoever produced it. Checking only that proves the document was not
altered in transit; it does not prove Alethia signed it. Binding the receipt's `key_id` to a
separately-served trusted key is what makes the difference, and a receipt signed by a key outside
that set fails — which is exactly what a forged receipt looks like.

The `Trust` field names the answer:

 Trust Meaning 
 --- --- 
 `pinned` verified against the key you supplied with `--key`/`--key-file` 
 `org` verified against your organization's own recorded signing key 
 `platform` verified against the Alethia platform key — attests "Alethia asserted this" 
 `self` only the receipt's own embedded key verified; who signed it is unestablished 

For verification that depends on nothing the control plane says about itself — the posture an
auditor or a security reviewer will want — pass the public key out of band

records.title: Verify Commands
records.heading: Exit status
records.text:
Exit status is part of the contract, so this can gate a pipeline:

 Situation Exit 
 --- --- 
 Signature verified against a vouched-for or pinned key `0` 
 The job carries no receipt non-zero 
 The receipt is unsigned (`algorithm: "none"`) non-zero, or `0` with `--allow-unsigned` 
 The signature does not match the receipt non-zero — **always**, no flag forgives it 
 The signature is valid but its key is not vouched for non-zero, or `0` with `--allow-untrusted` 

A receipt that fails its own signature check has been altered since it was signed. No flag
downgrades that.

Receipts are unsigned when the runner had no `ALETHIA_RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY` configured. That is a
legitimate state and the receipt still renders — but it is not evidence, so it fails by default.

records.title: Verify Commands
records.heading: alethia verify show
records.text:
Print the per-control report the receipt seals.

alethia verify show --job 4f3c2b1a-...
alethia verify show -j 4f3c2b1a-... -o json

 Flag Required Description 
 ------ ---------- ------------- 
 `--job`, `-j` Yes Job id. 

Verify: pass (aws, catalog elench-controls-0.5.2) — 14 pass, 0 fail, 0 warn, 1 not evaluable

Control Status Severity Title
KEYLESS-001 pass high No static cloud credentials
LEASTPRIV-001 pass high No wildcard admin policy
OIDC-001 not_evaluable medium OIDC trust is scoped

▸ OIDC-001 — OIDC trust is scoped
 coverage: no OIDC provider in the plan

Controls reporting `not_evaluable` are shown, never hidden. A control the engine could not inspect
is not a control that passed, and a report that quietly dropped them would overstate what was
checked. Any recorded waiver prints with who granted it, why, and when it expires.

`verify show` exits non-zero on a blocking verdict, matching `elench-verify`.

Add `-o json` for the full report object; `-o csv` emits the control rows.
