A refresh-only plan can only see resources that are **in state**. Resources that exist in the cloud but
were never provisioned by Alethia (true "unmanaged" resources) need a cloud inventory source (AWS Config,
GCP Cloud Asset Inventory) and are reported as not-yet-known rather than implied absent — the posture
never claims coverage it doesn't have.

records.title: Verification engine
records.text: Verification engine. How the deterministic policy gate works — the Evaluate seam, statuses, fail-closed gating, overrides, Access Analyzer corroboration, signed receipts, and drift.

records.title: Verification engine
records.heading: Verification engine
records.text:
The engine (`packages/core/verify`) is a deterministic policy gate over the OpenTofu **plan JSON**. It
runs **between `tofu plan` and `tofu apply`** inside `provisioner.RunDeployV2`, and it is **fail-closed**:
a hard control failure blocks the apply before any infrastructure changes.

records.title: Verification engine
records.heading: The Evaluate seam
records.text:
The whole engine sits behind one entrypoint:

func Evaluate(ctx context.Context, plan *tfjson.Plan) (*Report, error)

It is deterministic and side-effect free — the same plan always yields the same verdict, which is what
the evidence receipt relies on. The seam is **engine-agnostic**: Phase 0 ships a pure-Go evaluator
(builds and tests offline, no external policy runtime); an OPA/Rego backend for customer-authorable
control bundles can be swapped in behind the identical `Report` contract without touching any caller.

`EvaluateWithOptions(ctx, plan, opts)` is the same path with optional AWS Access Analyzer corroboration
(below).

records.title: Verification engine
records.heading: Three ways in — same Report
records.text:
The engine is plan-agnostic, so the same `Report` (and receipt) shape serves three inputs:

 Entrypoint Input Use 
 --- --- --- 
 `Evaluate(plan)` An Alethia-generated OpenTofu plan The apply-time gate. 
 `ParseCustomerPlan(json)` → `Evaluate` A **bring-your-own** `tofu show -json` plan Audit infrastructure Alethia didn't generate — **zero control changes**. 
 `EvaluateManifests(yaml)` Kubernetes manifests (multi-doc) The k8s [control set](/elench/control-catalog); `Provider` = `k8s`. 

The **"B" flow** (bring-your-own + audit) rides the latter two: an `AUDIT` job (migration `0052`) runs on
the runner (`executeAudit`) — parsing the customer's plan or manifests, evaluating them, and posting the
report to `jobs.execution_metadata.verify_result`. It provisions nothing; the console surfaces it through
the same `get_plan_result` tool + `VerifyBlock` a PLAN job's gate uses. Queue it with the
`audit_infrastructure` agent tool or the `queueAudit` action, or run it locally with
[`elench-verify -manifests`](/elench/extending).

records.title: Verification engine
records.heading: Statuses and the verdict
records.text:
Every control reports one of four statuses, and the report's overall verdict follows a strict
precedence:

 Status Meaning 
 --- --- 
 `pass` The control was evaluated and the plan satisfies it. 
 `fail` Evaluated and violated. On a real apply this **blocks** (unless overridden). 
 `warn` A recorded concern that does not block. 
 `not_evaluable` The plan JSON lacked the information to judge it. **Never** treated as a pass. 

> **Verdict precedence:** `fail` › `warn` › `not_evaluable` › `pass`.

The `not_evaluable` rung is the heart of the engine's honesty.

 
 **Never a silent pass.** A policy body that is computed until apply (`after_unknown`), or an
 AWS-managed policy referenced only by ARN (whose body is not in the plan), is reported `not_evaluable`
 with a plain-language coverage note — never a quiet `pass`. A silent pass on an un-inspectable
 resource is exactly the false result the verification claim must never make.

records.title: Verification engine
records.heading: Fail-closed, with a real exception path
records.text:
A fail-closed gate with no escape hatch gets disabled within a week. Elench ships the exception path
**with** the gate:

- A `verify.Override` is an **authorized, time-boxed** waiver of *specific* control ids — never a way to
 disable the gate wholesale.
- It is persisted on the deploy job (`jobs.verify_override`, migration `0043`), stamped server-side with
 the authorizing actor and an expiry by the `recordVerifyOverride` action.
- The runner reconstructs it (`buildVerifyOverride`) and passes it to the gate; `Report.Unwaived(ov)`
 returns any failing control the override does **not** cover. A non-empty result keeps the apply blocked.
- The waiver is recorded in the evidence receipt as an exception (who, why, expiry) — the verdict itself
 is **not** rewritten to pass.

records.title: Verification engine
records.heading: AWS IAM Access Analyzer corroboration
records.text:
Beyond the pattern checks, the gate can corroborate IAM policies with **AWS IAM Access Analyzer's
automated reasoning** — a *provable* statement about what a policy could grant, run pre-apply without
deploying anything.

- `verify.PolicyChecker` is the seam (the pure `verify` package carries no cloud SDK); the AWS-backed
 implementation lives in `packages/core/accessanalyzer` and calls `CheckAccessNotGranted` per action.
- Control `ACCESS-ANALYZER-001` fails when a planned policy could grant any action in a sensitive-action
 denylist; a checker error is `not_evaluable`, never a pass.
- It is **off by default** (no AWS calls). The runner enables it for AWS jobs when
 `ALETHIA_VERIFY_ACCESS_ANALYZER=1`, building the checker from the assumed-role config.

records.title: Verification engine
records.heading: Signed evidence receipt
records.text:
After the gate decides (and any override is applied), the runner seals a **`Receipt`** for the apply and
signs it (ed25519 detached signature → tamper-evident; offline `Verify`).

 
 

 Field Why 
 --- --- 
 `plan_sha256` Binds the receipt to the exact plan evaluated. 
 `tofu_version`, `catalog_version` A verdict is only meaningful against the schema + controls that produced it. 
 `report` The full per-control result, including `not_evaluable` and coverage. 
 `exception` Any recorded override (controls, reason, by, expiry). 
 `runner`, `evaluated_at` Provenance. 

 
 

A receipt signed by Alethia's own runner is **tamper-evidence on self-attestation** — it proves "Alethia's
runner asserted these controls passed on plan `sha256` and the file wasn't edited since", not independent
compliance proof. To make it meaningful to a customer's auditor, anchor the root of trust outside Alethia:
sign with a **customer-controlled key** and/or log the signature to a **transparency log (Rekor)**. The
key is loaded from `ALETHIA_RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY`; with none configured the receipt is attached
**unsigned** rather than blocking the apply — signing is additive evidence, not a precondition.

records.title: Verification engine
records.heading: Continuous drift — "keep proving it"
records.text:
`packages/core/drift` turns a `tofu plan -refresh-only -json` into a per-environment **`Posture`**
(`in_sync`, `drifted` count, per-resource `kind` ∈ modified/deleted/other) via `Analyze(plan)`. The full
loop is closed end-to-end:

 schedule] --> B[DETECT_DRIFT job migration 0044]
 B --> C[runner refresh-only → Analyze]
 C --> D[persist job-status route]
 D --> E[environment_drift 0051 · latest per env]
 E --> F[read get_drift_posture + MCP]
`} />

1. A tiered scheduler (`lib/drift/schedule` + `dispatch`) enqueues checks per environment on a cadence
 (production most often) through the cron route `/api/internal/drift/sweep` (`sweepDriftSchedule`).
2. `DETECT_DRIFT` (migration `0044`) runs on the runner (`executeDriftDetection`) and posts the `Posture`.
3. The job-status route persists it to **`environment_drift`** (migration `0051`, latest per environment)
 via `recordDriftPosture`.
4. `getLatestDriftPosture` reads it back for the UI, the assistant, and — via the
 [`get_drift_posture`](/elench/agent-runtime) tool (audience `both`) — external agents over MCP.

 
 **Coverage is stated, not hidden.** A refresh-only plan only sees resources in state, so it detects
 *modified* and *dele

records.title: Extending & running
records.text: Extending & running. Adding a control, the injection seams that keep AI advisory, the elench-verify CLI for CI, and the gated live exercises.

records.title: Extending & running
records.heading: Write the control
records.text:
Add a `control…` function in `packages/core/verify` returning a `ControlResult`. Use `resolveStatus` so
the pass / fail / warn / not_evaluable / vacuous-pass precedence stays consistent, and reuse the policy
helpers (`parseIAMPolicy`, `attrUnknown`, `toStringSlice`) — they already handle string-vs-array IAM
fields and unknown values.

records.title: Extending & running
records.heading: Add a fixture and a test
records.text:
Drop a plan-JSON fixture under `testdata/` and a case in the test suite. **Always include a
`not_evaluable` case** for any control that reads a body that can be computed — that path is the
engine's honesty guarantee.

records.title: Extending & running
records.heading: Bump the catalog version
records.text:
Change `CatalogVersion` whenever the new (or changed) control could alter a verdict. Old receipts are
only meaningful against the catalog that produced them.
 

 

A **Kubernetes** control is the same shape in `packages/core/verify/k8s.go`: add a `control…` function over
the decoded `k8sResource` list, wire it into `EvaluateManifests`, and add a fixture (an insecure manifest
→ fail, a clean one → pass). Reuse the `podSpec` / `containers` helpers.

records.title: Extending & running
records.heading: Adding a cloud
records.text:
Extending the provisioner + GitOps seam to a new cloud is a separate, documented checklist — the
`CloudProvider` impl, the OpenTofu template + keyless workload-identity outputs, runner credential
activation, and the per-cloud ArgoCD facts. See **[Multi-cloud](/elench/multi-cloud)** and
`packages/core/cloud/README.md`.

records.title: Extending & running
records.heading: The injection seams — "AI proposes, the gate disposes"
records.text:
Elench keeps AI strictly advisory through a set of injected interfaces, so the deterministic engine
always has the final say:

 Seam Role 
 --- --- 
 `PolicyChecker` AWS Access Analyzer corroboration (real implementation in `packages/core/accessanalyzer`). 
 `Remediator` Proposes a fix + re-plans; the loop only accepts a gate-confirmed result. 
 `SubAgentRunner` Runs one delegated colony task; the supervisor decides what to do with the outcome. 
 injected model call The LLM in `explainFindings` / the agent runner — swappable, so logic is tested with a fake. 

The safety spine is `ReVerify(original, candidatePlan)`: it re-runs the gate on a proposed fix and reports
which original failures it **resolved**, which **still fail**, and which it made **newly fail**. A fix is
`Accepted` only when every original failure is resolved with no regression. `RunRemediationLoop` wraps it
in a bounded harness so "AI proposes, the gate disposes" can never loop forever or apply an unverified fix.

records.title: Extending & running
records.heading: The elench-verify CLI
records.text:
`cmd/elench-verify` runs the gate over any plan JSON outside the runner — for local checks, CI gating, or
producing the go/no-go corpus measurement:

go build -o elench-verify ./packages/core/verify/cmd/elench-verify
tofu show -json tfplan elench-verify # human report; exit 2 if the verdict blocks
elench-verify -json plan.json # machine-readable report on stdout
elench-verify -manifests deploy.yaml # audit Kubernetes manifests instead of a plan

The default mode accepts a **bring-your-own** plan (via `ParseCustomerPlan`), not just an Alethia-generated
one — the same controls run either way. `-manifests` runs the k8s control set. Exit codes: `0`
pass/warn/not_evaluable · `2` blocking (fail) · `1` usage/parse error — so it drops straight into a CI step.

records.title: Extending & running
records.heading: Gated live exercises
records.text:
The deterministic logic is unit-tested with injected fakes; the live integrations are proven by **gated**
tests (skipped in normal CI, run explicitly) that exercise the real services end-to-end:

 
 

ELENCH_LIVE=1 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-… \
 pnpm -F console exec vitest run tests/lib/agent/llm-live.test.ts

Drives the supervisor → LLM sub-agent runner → **real Claude model** → parse → completion.

 
 

ELENCH_LIVE_AWS=1 AWS_REGION=us-east-1 \
 go test ./packages/core/accessanalyzer -run TestLive -v

Calls the **real `CheckAccessNotGranted` API**: an admin policy is reported as granting the denied
actions; a scoped policy grants none.

 
 

bash

records.title: Extending & running
records.heading: verify a real OpenTofu plan
records.text: tofu show -json plan.out elench-verify # blocks an admin policy (exit 2)

records.title: Extending & running
records.heading: remediation re-verify across two real plans
records.text:
ELENCH_PLAN_BAD=bad.json ELENCH_PLAN_FIXED=fixed.json \
 go test ./packages/core/verify -run TestLiveReVerifyRealPlans -v

`ReVerify(bad, fixed)` over genuine `tofu show -json` output resolves the failing control with no
regression (`accepted=true`).

 
 

 
 These tests stay **gated** so CI remains deterministic and never spends credits or hits a cloud; the
 env flags above run them on demand against real services.

records.title: Elench
records.text: Elench. The verification layer and agent harness — Alethia generates infrastructure and proves it, then keeps proving it.

records.title: Elench
records.heading: Elench
records.text:
**Elench** (Greek _elenchus_ — proof by cross-examination) is Alethia's verification layer and agent
harness. The thesis is simple: don't just generate infrastructure — **scrutinise it and produce
evidence**. Every change, human- or agent-initiated, runs through a deterministic gate between
`tofu plan` and `tofu apply`, and leaves a signed evidence receipt; drift re-checks keep proving it
after apply.

 
 **Honest framing.** Elench produces *evidence that named, versioned controls passed on a specific
 plan* — not a claim of "provably compliant" or "guaranteed least-privilege". A verdict is
 reproducible **given the same plan**; compliance is an auditor's judgment, not a property of one
 apply. The docs here are deliberately precise about what the engine can and cannot see.

records.title: Elench
records.heading: The load-bearing principle
records.text:
> The **deterministic engine is the trusted verdict. The LLM only proposes** — and every proposal is
> re-validated by that engine before it is trusted.

This division of labor runs through the whole system. The policy gate over the OpenTofu plan JSON is
pure, reproducible code. An LLM may explain a failing control or suggest a fix, but a suggested fix is
offered only if re-running the gate confirms it resolves the failure with no regression. The model is
never the gate and has no write path.

records.title: Elench
records.heading: Layered architecture
records.text:
native AI SDK MCP
 EXT --> remote MCP MCP
 MCP[Exposure — one adapter: remote MCP server read-only at launch]
 MCP --> CORE
 CORE[Elench core Tool Registry SSOT · agent-as-data runtime · supervisor]
 CORE --> calls ACT[Platform actions PDP-gated]
 CORE --> calls VER[Verification engine plan-JSON gate · override · signed receipt · drift]
 VER --> new verify stage RUN[Go runner · OpenTofu]
`} />

Two halves, joined at the runner:

- **The verification engine** (`packages/core/verify`, `packages/core/drift`,
 `packages/core/accessanalyzer`) — the deterministic gate, the signed receipt, and continuous drift.
 This is the headline.
- **The agent harness** (`apps/console/lib/ai/tools`, `lib/agent/*`, `app/api/mcp`) — one tool registry
 exposed read-only to external agents, scoped per-agent identities with isolated memory, and a
 supervisor that delegates to a colony of sub-agents.

Start with the **[Architecture](/elench/architecture)** page for the full repos → verified-GitOps-cluster
system (the "A" infer-and-generate flow and the "B" bring-your-own + audit flow); the pages below go deep

 **Two things share the name "Elench."** These pages are the engine + harness **internals**. For the
 in-console **assistant** — its workspaces, knowledge base, dashboards, and artifacts, written for

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.text: Multi-cloud. How AWS, GCP and Azure all deploy apps — the cloud-agnostic GitOps seam, per-cloud workload identity, manifest generation, and the checklist for adding a cloud.

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.heading: Multi-cloud GitOps seam
records.text:
The provisioner was already ~95% cloud-agnostic — the `CloudProvider` interface, `ProviderTfvars`, and
`ConfigureKubeconfig` all work for AWS, GCP and Azure. The **one** thing keeping GCP/Azure from actually
*deploying apps* was the GitOps seam: `argocd.BuildFromOutputs` + the ArgoCD templates were
AWS/IRSA/EKS-hardcoded. That seam is now `Provider`-discriminated, so all three clouds render a working
ArgoCD layer.

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.heading: Cloud-agnostic InfraFacts
records.text:
`packages/core/argocd/infra_facts.go` carries **common facts** (cluster name/endpoint, region, DNS) plus a
**per-cloud workload-identity block**, and `BuildFromOutputs` extracts the right outputs per provider:

 Provider Cluster output Workload identity external-dns SA annotation 
 --- --- --- --- 
 AWS `eks_cluster_name` IRSA role ARN `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` 
 GCP `gke_cluster_name` Workload Identity SA email (`external_dns_service_account`) `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account` 
 Azure `aks_cluster_name` Federated Identity client id (`external_dns_client_id`) `azure.workload.identity/client-id` 

`InfraFacts.DNSProvider()` maps the cloud to the external-dns `provider` value (`aws` / `google` /
`azure`). The ArgoCD templates (`infra/templates/argocd/*.yaml`) switch on `.Provider`; AWS-only apps
(`aws-load-balancer-controller`, `karpenter`, `storage-class-gp3`) are guarded so they **render empty →
are skipped** on other clouds. `render_test.go` pins AWS-unchanged and asserts the GCP/Azure output.

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.heading: Per-cloud workload identity, keyless
records.text:
Each cloud binds the in-cluster `external-dns` service account to a cloud identity with **no static key**:

- **GCP** — `infra/templates/project/gcp/workload-identity.tf`: a Google service account with `roles/dns.admin`,
 bound to `external-dns/external-dns-sa` via GKE Workload Identity; exported as `external_dns_service_account`.
- **Azure** — `azure/workload-identity.tf`: a user-assigned managed identity + a **federated credential** on
 the AKS OIDC issuer (`oidc_issuer_url` output added to the AKS module), `DNS Zone Contributor`; exported as
 `external_dns_client_id`.

Both templates are `tofu validate`-clean.

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.heading: Manifest generation (the "generate" apps path)
records.text:
`packages/core/manifests` renders a hardened Deployment/Service/Ingress per detected service
(`FromServices` → `WriteManifests`): non-root, `drop: [ALL]`, read-only rootfs, resource limits, no
privilege escalation — so the generated manifests **pass the k8s [audit](/elench/control-catalog) by
construction**. At deploy, `RunDeployV2` commits them to the GitOps repo **only when the repo has no
manifests yet** (`hasManifests` guard):

 
 **Never clobbers bring-your-own.** Generation is safe-by-construction: it writes to an *empty* apps repo
 or does nothing, and is **non-fatal** — a git edge case warns, it never fails an otherwise-healthy
 cluster. "Bring your own manifests" simply means ArgoCD points at a repo that already has them.

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.heading: Adding a cloud
records.text:
The deploy flow itself never changes — a new cloud is five edits (mirrors
`packages/core/cloud/README.md`):

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.heading: CloudProvider impl + factory case
records.text: Add ` _provider.go` implementing the four-method interface and a `case` in `NewCloudProvider`.

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.heading: OpenTofu template + outputs
records.text:
Provision a cluster + backing services + a **keyless** workload-identity binding for the external-dns KSA,
exporting the identity. Validate with `tofu validate`.

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.heading: Runner credential activation
records.text: Teach the runner how to activate the cloud's credentials before `tofu` runs (AssumeRole / WIF / federated).

records.title: Multi-cloud
records.heading: ArgoCD facts + templates
records.text:
Add a `BuildFromOutputs` case + the per-cloud block, and the branch in `external-dns.yaml` (provider value
+ SA annotation). Empty render = "not applicable".
 
 

 
 **Honest status.** The seam is green — `BuildFromOutputs` per-cloud unit tests, template render tests,
 and `tofu validate` for the GCP/Azure workload-identity OpenTofu. The remaining proof is a real
 GKE/AKS end-to-end run + a live apps-repo git push; only a live cluster/repo can validate those.

records.title: Receipts & signing
records.text: Receipts & signing. What an evidence receipt is, how ed25519 signing makes it tamper-evident and offline-verifiable, waivers, and the root-of-trust model.

records.title: Receipts & signing
records.heading: Receipts & signing
records.text:
An **evidence receipt** is the record Alethia seals on every apply. It is the artifact that turns "the
console says it passed" into something you can verify independently, later, without trusting the console.

records.title: Receipts & signing
records.heading: What a receipt binds
records.text:
Each receipt is bound to the exact change it describes:

- **`plan_sha256`** — the hash of the exact OpenTofu plan that was applied.
- **verdict** — the elench gate's decision (`pass` / `warn` / `fail` / `not_evaluable`).
- **catalog version** — which control catalog produced the verdict (an old receipt is only meaningful
 against the catalog that generated it).
- the full per-control report, the provider, OpenTofu version, the runner, and the evaluation time.
- any **sealed exception** (see waivers below).

records.title: Receipts & signing
records.heading: Signing — what it buys you
records.text:
When a signing key is configured, the receipt is signed with **ed25519**. A signed receipt is
**tamper-evident** and **verifiable offline**: anyone with the public key can confirm the receipt wasn't
altered after the fact — the signature is over the receipt's canonical JSON, so any change breaks it. Even
with the platform-held key, this upgrades "trust the database row" to "cryptographically bound to this
plan and verdict."

 State Meaning 
 --- --- 
 **Signed** An ed25519 signature seals the receipt; it's tamper-evident and offline-verifiable. 
 **Unsigned** A receipt was sealed, but no signing key is configured — still a faithful record, not signed. 
 **—** No apply has sealed a receipt for this environment yet.

records.title: Receipts & signing
records.heading: Enabling signing
records.text:
Signing is off until a key is set. Provide an ed25519 key to the runner (via
`ALETHIA_RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY`) and every subsequent receipt is signed. Absent a key, receipts are still
attached — just unsigned — so an apply is never blocked on signing.

records.title: Receipts & signing
records.heading: Checking one yourself
records.text:
alethia verify receipt --job 

Pulls the receipt, checks its signature, and **exits non-zero when it cannot** — so a deployment
pipeline can gate on it. `alethia verify show --job ` prints the per-control report behind
the verdict. See [Verify Commands](/cli/commands/verify).

The signature is checked against a key the control plane **vouches for**, not against the public key
the receipt carries about itself. That distinction is the whole point: a receipt always verifies
under its own embedded key, whoever produced it, so checking only that would prove the document was
not altered — never who signed it. To verify against a key you hold out of band, pass
`--key-file `.

records.title: Receipts & signing
records.heading: Root of trust
records.text:
A receipt signed by Alethia's own runner attests "Alethia asserted this" — `alethia verify receipt`
reports that honestly as trust `platform`, and reports `org` when your own registered key signed it.
For auditor-grade non-repudiation, sign with a **customer-controlled key** and/or anchor the receipt
in a **transparency log** (Rekor) so its existence and integrity are provable by any third party
offline. Both are on the roadmap; the signing seam is already in place.

records.title: Receipts & signing
records.heading: Waivers
records.text:
A fail-closed gate blocks an apply on a hard failure. A **waiver** (override) is the authorized, escape
hatch: a time-boxed pass of **specific** failing control IDs, recorded with who granted it, why, and when
it expires. The waiver is sealed into the receipt as an **exception**, so the record shows the gate was
passed deliberately — not disabled. Active waivers are listed on the Evidence page.

records.title: Security scanning
records.text: Security scanning. How Alethia rolls up in-cluster vulnerability findings from Trivy-Operator, and what "Not scanned" means on the Evidence page.

records.title: Security scanning
records.heading: Security scanning
records.text:
The Evidence page's **Security** column reports the vulnerability posture of the workloads running in an
environment's cluster. The data is real — it comes from [Trivy-Operator](https://aquasecurity.github.io/trivy-operator/),
read live from the cluster — never a synthetic all-clear.

records.title: Security scanning
records.heading: How it works
records.text:
When Alethia inspects a cluster (on the deploy finalizer and on the day-2 drift refresh), it reads the
Trivy-Operator `VulnerabilityReport` custom resources across all namespaces and sums the findings by
severity — **critical / high / medium / low** — along with the number of reports that fed the aggregate.
That rollup is stored per environment and surfaced as the Security posture.

records.title: Security scanning
records.heading: What the Evidence page shows
records.text:
Mark Meaning 
 --- --- 
 **N critical** / **N high** The highest-severity findings across the cluster's Trivy reports. 
 **N low** Only medium/low findings remain. 
 **Clean** Trivy scanned and found no critical/high/medium/low vulnerabilities. 
 **Not scanned** Trivy-Operator isn't installed (or has produced no reports yet) — an honest unknown.

records.title: Security scanning
records.heading: Enabling scans
records.text:
"Not scanned" means the **Trivy-Operator add-on** isn't running in the cluster. Install it from the add-on
marketplace; once it produces `VulnerabilityReport`s, the next cluster inspection picks them up and the
Security posture fills in automatically. Nothing to wire on the Alethia side — if the reports exist,
Alethia reads them.

records.title: Architecture
records.text: Architecture. How isolated execution works — the per-job container, the environment allowlist, PID and network isolation, the state-proxy source-drop, per-job and per-VM tokens, and default-deny domain-allowlist egress.

records.title: Architecture
records.heading: Architecture
records.text:
Isolated execution is a **seam** in the runner (`packages/core/sandbox`): the runner calls `Sandbox.Run`
instead of invoking the provisioner directly, and a backend decides how much isolation the work gets. Trusted
templates use the in-process `Passthrough` backend; untrusted bring-your-own on the managed fleet uses the
`Container` backend described here.

 
 This page is the customer/operator view. The full engineering reference — types, the re-exec contract, the
 allowlist tables, and the shipped dependency chain — lives in the
 [`packages/core/sandbox` README](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs/blob/main/packages/core/sandbox/README.md).

records.title: Architecture
records.heading: The per-job container
records.text:
A container can't run a Go closure, so the runner **serializes** the work and **re-execs itself** inside a
fresh per-job container. The child reconstructs the exact work from a serialized stage
(`deploy` / `plan` / `destroy` / `drift` / `chart_scan` / `iac_scan`), runs it, and writes its result back into the per-job working
directory for the parent to read. One job, one container, torn down after — the fleet VM itself is disposable
(one job per VM).

Hardening on the container: dropped Linux capabilities, no-new-privileges, its own PID namespace (so it
cannot read the parent runner's `/proc`), only the per-job workdir mounted writable, and pid/memory
limits.

records.title: Architecture
records.heading: The environment allowlist (and a fail-closed guard)
records.text:
The child gets **only** an allowlisted set of environment variables:

- the cloud-auth vars the credential activators set — file paths and non-secret ids (`AWS_CONFIG_FILE` /
 `AWS_PROFILE`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `ARM_*` / `AZURE_*`, `ALIBABA_CLOUD_*`),
- the token-cloud tokens the provider needs (e.g. `HCLOUD_TOKEN`),
- the state-proxy auth and the egress-proxy vars,
- a minimal toolchain (`PATH`, locale).

Everything else — the runner token, the storage master key, the receipt-signing key, static cloud keys — is
**dropped**. A **fail-closed guard** runs on the final child environment and refuses to start the container
if any denylisted secret survived, so a mistake that widens the allowlist is caught *before* untrusted code
runs. Credentials that are files are mounted **read-only** at their original paths (as directories, so the
runner's ~5-minute token refresh stays visible to a long `apply`).

records.title: Architecture
records.heading: Removing secrets at the source
records.text:
The container can only contain what it isn't handed. Three source-drops keep the allowlist short and the
fleet's boot configuration secret-free:

- **OpenTofu state via a console proxy, not storage keys.** Project templates use an `http` backend pointed
 at the console; auth is a **per-job, key-scoped** token, and the state object key is derived server-side
 from the job. The runner never holds an object-storage credential, and one job's token can only reach its
 own state.
- **Per-job cloud tokens.** Cloud credentials are minted per job and bound to it — a stolen runner token
 can't mint another cloud's credentials.
- **Per-VM bootstrap tokens.** Each fleet VM self-registers with its own short-TTL, instance-bound token
 rather than a shared fleet secret.

Together these mean a managed VM's boot configuration carries no long-lived secret — so the network control
below closes the *last* read rather than being the only line of defense.

records.title: Architecture
records.heading: Network: default-deny + domain allowlist
records.text:
The untrusted child has **no network route of its own**. On the managed fleet:

- the VM runs an internal-only network (no gateway → no route off the box) plus a **forward proxy** that
 allowlists egress **by domain** (registries, Git hosts, the target cloud's API);
- the runner — and the child, which inherits the runner's network namespace — reach the internet *only*
 through that proxy;
- so the cloud metadata service (`169.254.169.254`) and arbitrary exfiltration endpoints are **unreachable by
 construction**, not merely blocked by a rule.

A `chart_scan` stage needs no network at all and runs fully **deny-all** (`--network none`) with zero secrets.

The backend is **fail-closed on managed**: it refuses to run untrusted work unless egress enforcement is
confirmed on the fleet — it never silently falls back to running unsandboxed.

records.title: Architecture
records.heading: Where to go next
records.text:
The trust model, the guarantees, and availability.

records.title: Configuration
records.text: Configuration. The ALETHIA_SANDBOX_* runner environment variables that select the isolation backend and set its runtime, image, network, egress, memory, and cancellation grace.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Configuration
records.text:
The per-job container sandbox is configured entirely through `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_*` environment
variables read by the **runner**. This page is the reference for those variables — what each one
selects, its default, and the accepted values.

 
 These variables are read on the runner, and the container backend applies only to **untrusted
 bring-your-own** work on the managed fleet. The default backend (`Passthrough`) ignores most of
 them. For the enabling sequence on the fleet, see the
 [managed provisioning runbook](/self-hosting/managed-provisioning).

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Backend selection
records.text:
`ALETHIA_SANDBOX_BACKEND` picks the isolation backend:

- `container` selects the per-job `Container` backend.
- Any other value (including unset) selects the in-process `Passthrough` backend — no isolation.

When `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_BACKEND=container` is set but the container backend fails to initialize on a
runner whose operator is not `self`, selection is **fail-closed**: the runner falls back to a
`Passthrough` that refuses every job rather than silently running untrusted work unsandboxed.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: The container variables
records.text:
These variables configure the `Container` backend. They are parsed by `NewContainerFromEnv`.

 Variable Default Meaning 
 --- --- --- 
 `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_RUNTIME` `docker` The container CLI to invoke (`docker` for local dev, `podman` for the fleet). The value must resolve on `PATH`, or the backend fails to initialize. 
 `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_IMAGE` the runner's own image ref (`ALETHIA_RUNNER_IMAGE`) The image the per-job container runs. If both this and `ALETHIA_RUNNER_IMAGE` are empty, the backend returns an error — an image is required. 
 `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_NETWORK` runtime default The container `--network` value. Empty uses the runtime's default network. 
 `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_EGRESS_ENFORCED` unset (false) Confirms that the runtime constrains egress. The managed fail-closed gate requires it (see below). 
 `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_MEMORY` `2g` The container `--memory` limit. 

 
 The per-job container pid limit is fixed at 512 and is not configurable through an environment
 variable.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Cancellation grace
records.text:
`ALETHIA_CANCEL_GRACE_SECONDS` sets the `SIGINT`→`SIGKILL` grace window applied when a running job
is cancelled mid-flight. The value is an integer number of seconds:

- Unset defaults to 120 seconds.
- A value of `0` sends `SIGKILL` immediately after `SIGINT`.

The grace window lets a foreground container runtime forward the interrupt to OpenTofu, so the
in-flight resource finishes, state is written, and the state lock is released before the process
exits.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Enforcing isolation on the default backend
records.text:
`ALETHIA_SANDBOX_ENFORCE_MANAGED` is the kill-switch for the default (`Passthrough`) path. When it
is set, a `Passthrough` backend **refuses** to run on any runner whose operator is not `self`,
instead of silently running unsandboxed. It never refuses a `self` operator, and when it is unset
(the default) the `Passthrough` backend never refuses at all.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Truthy values
records.text:
`ALETHIA_SANDBOX_EGRESS_ENFORCED` and `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_ENFORCE_MANAGED` are boolean flags. They are
read as true for any of these values (case-insensitive):

1
true
yes
on

Any other value — including unset — is read as false.

records.title: Configuration
records.heading: Fail-closed behavior
records.text:
Two gates depend on the variables above:

- **Managed egress gate.** On an `operator=managed` runner, the container backend refuses to run an
 egress-permitted stage unless `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_EGRESS_ENFORCED` is true. A no-egress stage (such
 as `chart_scan`, which runs with `--network none`) is exempt.
- **Backend fallback.** Requesting `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_BACKEND=container` on a non-`self` runner where
 the backend cannot initialize yields a refusing `Passthrough`, never an unsandboxed run.

records.title: Isolated Execution
records.text: Isolated Execution. When Alethia runs your bring-your-own OpenTofu/Terraform or Helm on the managed fleet, each job runs in a per-job sealed sandbox — no shared secrets, no cloud metadata, default-deny domain-allowlisted egress.

records.title: Isolated Execution
records.heading: Isolated Execution
records.text:
Zero-credential connections control **who** can touch a cloud. Isolated execution controls what the
**provisioning code itself** can do once it runs. When Alethia runs *your* code — bring-your-own OpenTofu/Terraform
providers, `external` data sources, Helm charts and their hooks — on the **managed fleet**, that code is
arbitrary. Isolated execution is the boundary that runs it **sealed off** from the platform.

 
 **What this is — and isn't.** This is the isolation boundary that makes *managed bring-your-own execution*
 safe: a per-job sandbox with an allowlisted environment and a locked-down network. It is **not** a
 general-purpose "spin up a sandbox and run anything" service, and there is no customer-invokable sandbox API
 today — a customer-facing sandbox/preview surface is on the roadmap. What ships now is the **guarantee**
 underneath managed BYO: your code can't reach the platform's secrets, the cloud metadata service, or the
 open internet.

records.title: Isolated Execution
records.heading: The trust model
records.text:
Alethia runs two kinds of code, and treats them differently:

- **Trusted templates** — Alethia's own project templates (EKS / GKE / AKS / ACK / Talos + supporting
 services). Reviewed platform code, so it runs in-process on the runner. This is every managed provision
 today.
- **Untrusted bring-your-own** — your OpenTofu/Terraform or Helm. Arbitrary code, so on the managed fleet it runs in a
 **per-job container sandbox**: a fresh container per job, its own PID namespace, an allowlisted environment
 (no runner token, no storage key, no signing key — only the short-lived, job-scoped cloud credentials the
 job actually needs), read-only credential mounts, and a **default-deny, domain-allowlisted** network.

The container is what actually contains a hostile provider. Scrubbing environment variables at the last
moment does **not** — a child process sharing the worker's PID namespace can just read the parent's
`/proc/1/environ`. Only a real uid / pid / net namespace boundary contains it.

records.title: Isolated Execution
records.heading: The guarantees
records.text:
For an untrusted job on the managed fleet:

 Guarantee How 
 --- --- 
 **No platform secrets** The child gets an allowlist-only environment; a fail-closed guard refuses to start the container if any platform secret (runner token, storage key, signing key) would leak in. 
 **No cross-job state** OpenTofu state goes through a console **state proxy** with a per-job, key-scoped token — one job's token can only touch its own state. The runner holds no object-storage credential. 
 **No cloud metadata** The child has no network route of its own; it reaches only a domain-allowlist forward proxy, so `169.254.169.254` (which serves the VM's boot config) is unreachable by construction. 
 **No open egress** Only the registries, Git hosts, and the target cloud's API are reachable — everything else is default-denied. 
 **No host reach** Its own PID namespace, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, resource limits.

records.title: Isolated Execution
records.heading: Why it matters
records.text:
Alethia sits in the gap between IaC orchestrators (which run *your IaC* on shared workers) and BYOC PaaSes
(which run *your apps*). Running **bring-your-own infrastructure code in a per-job sealed sandbox** is the
execution-trust complement to the [zero-credential](/concepts/security) connection model — and the safety
floor under the "proof, not just generation" story ([Elench](/elench) verifies *what* the change does; this
contains *how* it runs).

records.title: Isolated Execution
records.heading: Availability
records.text:
Isolated execution applies to the **managed fleet**. Bring-your-own Helm/IaC is gated by
`ALETHIA_BYO_HELM_ENABLED` and, until the container backend is enabled and verified on the fleet, stays
trusted-templates-only. Operators turn it on per the
[managed provisioning runbook](/self-hosting/managed-provisioning#untrusted-byo-container-sandbox-3b).

records.text: Internal Architecture. Main loop, heartbeat mechanism, graceful shutdown, and the core shared package.

records.title: Internal Architecture
records.heading: Internal Architecture
records.text: Runner is a single Go binary with a straightforward architecture: a main poll loop, a heartbeat goroutine, and shared libraries from the `core` package.

records.title: Internal Architecture
records.heading: Main Loop
records.text:
Reg[Register with Alethia API]
 Reg --> HB[Start heartbeat goroutine · every 30s]
 Reg --> Wake[Start wake-stream goroutine · SSE /api/runners/wake]
 Reg --> Poll{Claim loop · on wake or 30s safety poll POST /api/jobs/claim}
 Wake --> wake Poll
 Poll --> no job Wait[await next wake / safety tick]
 Wait --> Poll
 Poll --> job claimed Mint[Mint per-job cloud creds · keyless OIDC]
 Mint --> Exec[Execute via sandbox seam · tofu, ArgoCD]
 Exec --> Logs[Stream logs]
 Logs --> Report[Report result]
 Report --> Poll
`} />

The claim loop runs on the main goroutine; the wake-stream listener and the heartbeat each run as a
background goroutine. All share the runner configuration.

Provisioning work runs through the **sandbox seam** (`packages/core/sandbox`), not by invoking the provisioner
directly. For trusted Alethia templates the default `Passthrough` backend runs it in-process; on the managed
fleet, untrusted bring-your-own IaC/Helm runs in a per-job **container** with an allowlisted environment and a
locked-down network. See the [`sandbox` package README](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethialabs/blob/main/packages/core/sandbox/README.md)
and [Security Architecture → Execution isola

records.title: Internal Architecture
records.heading: Job types
records.text:
The dispatch switch (`internal/agent/runner.go`) routes each claimed job to its handler:

 Job type Handler Does 
 --- --- --- 
 `PLAN` / `DEPLOY` / `DESTROY` `executePlan` / `executeDeploy` / … OpenTofu plan/apply/destroy (+ the verify gate, ArgoCD, and manifest scaffold on deploy). Routed through the **sandbox seam**. 
 `CHART_SCAN` `executeChartScan` Render a bring-your-own Helm chart to manifests + scan it (zero secrets, deny-all egress) — always sandboxed. 
 `ANALYZE_REPO` `executeAnalyzeRepo` Clone + statically scan a repo into a `RepoDigest`. 
 `DETECT_DRIFT` `executeDriftDetection` `tofu plan -refresh-only` → `drift.Analyze` → post a `Posture`. 
 `AUDIT` `executeAudit` Run the elench verify engine over a **bring-your-own** plan or k8s manifests → post `verify_result`. Provisions nothing. 
 `IAC_SCAN` `executeIacScan` Static scan of bring-your-own IaC — always sandboxed. 
 `STATE_SURGERY` `executeStateSurgery` Operator-driven tofu state repair (ships **inert** / fail-closed). 
 `PROBE_CLUSTER` `executeProbeCluster` Live cluster-alive probe → writes `environment_probes`. 
 `BUILD` `executeBuild` Image build & push — schedules kaniko Jobs in the customer's cluster → `execution

records.title: Internal Architecture
records.heading: Configuration
records.text:
Runner receives its configuration via environment variables:

 Variable Description 
 ---------- ------------- 
 `ALETHIA_WEB_ORIGIN` Base URL of the Alethia instance 
 `ALETHIA_RUNNER_ID` Unique Runner identifier (assigned at registration) 
 `ALETHIA_RUNNER_TOKEN` Authentication token for API calls 
 `ALETHIA_RUNNER_OPERATOR` `managed` or `self` (the legacy `ALETHIA_RUNNER_MODE` with `cloud-hosted`/`self-hosted` still works as a back-compat fallback) 
 `INFRACOST_API_KEY` Optional, for cost estimation 

The runner holds **no object-storage credentials**. tofu state goes through the console **state proxy**
(`backend "http"` → `/api/jobs/{id}/state`) authenticated by a per-job token in `TF_HTTP_PASSWORD`, and cloud
auth is minted per job via keyless OIDC — so a managed fleet VM's cloud-init carries no long-lived secret.
Managed fleet VMs additionally self-register with a per-VM, short-TTL bootstrap token rather than any static
credential.

records.title: Internal Architecture
records.heading: Heartbeat Mechanism
records.text:
The heartbeat goroutine sends `POST /api/runners/heartbeat` every 30 seconds. The payload carries:

- The runner version
- The cloud providers this runner can claim (per-cloud routing)

The runner's identity travels in the `X-Runner-ID` / `X-Runner-Token` headers, not the body. The
response returns any server-side-cancelled job IDs (`cancelled_job_ids`) — the fallback cancel path
when a wake-stream cancel was missed.

Alethia uses the heartbeat to:
- Mark Runners as ONLINE (heartbeat within 60s) or OFFLINE (heartbeat missed)
- Detect dead Runners and requeue their jobs
- Track which Runner is running which job

If a Runner crashes mid-job:
1. Heartbeat stops arriving
2. After 60 seconds, Alethia marks the Runner OFFLINE
3. If no log updates for 5+ minutes, the job is marked FAILED
4. User can retry the job — tofu state is preserved in the console state proxy (`project-tofu-state`, with fenced locks so a reclaimed lock can't clobber a slow writer)

records.title: Internal Architecture
records.heading: Graceful Shutdown
records.text:
When Runner receives SIGINT or SIGTERM:

1. Enters a local **draining** state — stops claiming new jobs
2. Lets the in-flight job (if any) run to completion, up to a 10-minute grace period, after which the
 context is cancelled to force shutdown
3. Exits

In the managed fleet, a warm-pool VM claims jobs until the scaler decides it is surplus. Scale-down
is a two-step **drain then destroy**: the controller marks the runner `DRAINING` (it stops claiming
but finishes its in-flight job), and the next tick destroys it once idle — so the SIGTERM the VM
sends always lands on a runner that already drained gracefully. See
[Warm-pool scaling](/runner/scale-to-zero). (Self-operated runners get the same on any orchestrator's
stop signal.)

records.title: Internal Architecture
records.heading: API Client
records.text:
The `RunnerAPIClient` handles all communication with Alethia:

 Method Endpoint Purpose 
 -------- ---------- --------- 
 `ClaimJob()` `POST /api/jobs/claim` Atomic job claiming 
 `Heartbeat()` `POST /api/runners/heartbeat` Keepalive 
 `UpdateJobStatus()` `PUT /api/jobs/{id}/status` Status transitions 
 `SendLog()` `POST /api/jobs/{id}/logs` Log batch delivery 
 `UploadPlanArtifact()` `POST /api/jobs/{id}/plan-artifact` Plan JSON upload 
 `DownloadPlanArtifact()` `GET /api/jobs/{id}/plan-artifact` Plan JSON download 

All requests include `X-Runner-ID` and `X-Runner-Token` headers for authentication.

records.title: Internal Architecture
records.heading: Shared core Package
records.text:
Runner and Alethia CLI both import from `packages/core/`:

 Package Purpose 
 --------- --------- 
 `provisioner/` Bootstrap, deploy, destroy orchestration 
 `tofu/` OpenTofu CLI wrapper (init, plan, apply, destroy) — drives the `tofu` binary via `terraform-exec`

 `sandbox/` The per-job isolation seam (Passthrough / Container backends)

 `cloud/azure_provider.go` Azure federated-auth provider tfvars + kubeconfig

This shared package ensures both the CLI and Runner use the same provisioning logic.

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.text: Cloud Credential Management. How Runner assumes temporary credentials per job — AWS, Alibaba, GCP, and Azure, plus token clouds (DigitalOcean / Hetzner / Civo) with an optional self-managed path where the token never leaves your infrastructure.

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.heading: Cloud Credential Management
records.text: Runner assumes temporary cloud credentials at the start of every job and clears them when the job completes. No credentials persist between jobs.

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.heading: Per-job credential lifecycle
records.text:
B[Read cloud_identity from the claim]
 B --> C[Provider-specific keyless minting]
 C --> D[Set env vars · OIDC token file]
 D --> E[Execute tofu · reads env vars]
 E --> F[defer: clear credentials + remove token file]
`} />

The `defer` ensures credentials and any on-disk assertion are always cleared, even if the job fails
or panics.

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.heading: AWS: keyless AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
records.text:
**Input from cloud_identity:**
- `role_arn` — ARN of the IAM role in the user's AWS account (its trust policy trusts the Alethia issuer)

**Execution (managed runner — keyless, no ambient AWS identity):** the runner mints a web-identity assertion
(audience `sts.amazonaws.com`) from the console and writes a single AWS profile that federates **straight into
the customer role** — no platform account, no ExternalId:

[profile alethia-customer]
web_identity_token_file = /tmp/alethia-aws-XXXX/web-identity-token
role_arn = arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AlethiaProvisionerRole
role_session_name = alethia-runner

It points OpenTofu's aws provider at that profile (`AWS_CONFIG_FILE` + `AWS_PROFILE=alethia-customer`). A
background refresher re-mints the assertion into the token **file** every few minutes; the SDK re-reads it
and re-assumes on session expiry, so a `tofu apply` longer than the ~1 hour session keeps a live assertion
(parity with GCP/Azure/Alibaba). No access key ever reaches the runner (see
[Security Architecture → AWS](/concepts/security#aws-keyless-issuer-direct-iam-role)).

**Self-operated runners** (`operator=self`) run in the customer's own cloud with their own ambient
crede

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.heading: Alibaba Cloud: RAM Role via OIDC (keyless, account-free)
records.text:
Alibaba is **keyless** — there is no platform AccessKey (the old `ALETHIA_ALIBABA_ACCESS_KEY_*` was
retired). The runner authenticates the same way the console does: an anonymous **`AssumeRoleWithOIDC`**
using a short-lived assertion minted by the Alethia issuer. Alethia holds no Alibaba account.

**Input from cloud_identity:**
- `role_arn` — ARN of the RAM role in the user's account (`acs:ram:: :role/ `)
- `oidc_provider_arn` — ARN of the customer's RAM OIDC provider (fixed name `alethia`)

**Execution:**

func ActivateAlibabaOIDC(ctx, fetcher, roleArn, oidcProviderArn string) (cleanup func(), err error) {
 token, err := fetcher.FetchAlibabaToken() // mint an assertion from the console (/api/runners/alibaba-token)
 tokenFile := writeToTempFile(token)

 // The alicloud provider runs AssumeRoleWithOIDC itself from these — no AccessKey on the runner.
 os.Setenv("ALIBABA_CLOUD_ROLE_ARN", roleArn)
 os.Setenv("ALIBABA_CLOUD_OIDC_PROVIDER_ARN", oidcProviderArn)
 os.Setenv("ALIBABA_CLOUD_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE", tokenFile)
 // …a background refresher re-mints into tokenFile every ~5 min; cleanup stops it + removes the file
 return cleanup, nil
}

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.heading: Azure: Federated Identity

Azure is **keyless** — no client secret reaches the runner. The runner authenticates **as the customer's
user-assigned managed identity** (there is no platform Entra app) by fetching a short-lived OIDC assertion
from the console (the console holds the issuer signing key) and handing it to OpenTofu as the client

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.heading: Token Clouds: DigitalOcean / Hetzner / Civo
records.text:
These providers have no cross-account role federation — they authenticate with a single API token.
Alethia supports two models.

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.heading: Stored scoped token (encrypted)
records.text:
The customer pastes a scoped API token; Alethia stores it **encrypted at rest** and decrypts it only at
claim time, passing it to the runner. The runner exports the provider's env var
(`DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN` / `HCLOUD_TOKEN` / `CIVO_TOKEN`) for the job and clears it after.

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.heading: Self-managed — token stays in your infrastructure (true zero-trust)
records.text:
For clouds without federation, the honest zero-trust path: the token lives **only** in your self-hosted
runner's environment, never in Alethia's database.

- The connection is recorded with `self_managed: true` and **no token**.
- Its jobs are flagged `requires_self_runner`, and `claim_next_job` **excludes managed runners** from
 them — so only *your* runner, which holds `HCLOUD_TOKEN` / `CIVO_TOKEN` / `DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN`
 in its own env, can claim and run them.
- The runner reads the token from its environment (the `selfManaged` path) and never receives it from
 Alethia.

Pick the model in the connect sheet: **"Store a scoped token"** (encrypted at rest) vs **"Self-hosted
runner — token stays in your infra."** See [Self-operated runners](/runner/self-hosted).

records.title: Cloud Credential Management
records.heading: Security Properties
records.text:
Property Guarantee 
 ---------- ----------- 
 No persistent credentials Env vars are cleared after every job via `defer` 
 No credential sharing Each job gets its own assumed session 
 Time-bounded AWS sessions expire after 1 hour 
 Scoped Credentials only have permissions defined in the IAM role / service account / app registration 
 Revocable User deletes the IAM role / WIF config / App Registration → instant revocation 
 No file leaks Temporary credential files are deleted in `defer` cleanup 
 Optional zero-storage Self-managed token clouds keep the secret in your runner's env — it never enters Alethia's database

records.heading: provisioner/
records.text:
The main orchestration layer. Entry point: `RunDeployV2()`.

 B[Write backend HCL · console HTTP proxy]
 B --> C[Generate tfvars · OverrideTfvarsFromMap]
 C --> D[tofu init]
 D --> E[tofu plan]
 E --> F[verify gate · verify.Evaluate]
 F --> hard fail unwaived X[refuse before apply]
 F --> pass / warn / waived G[attach signed receipt]
 G --> H[tofu apply]
 H --> I[write keyless kubeconfig · runner kube-token]
 I --> J[install ArgoCD · reachability gate]
 J --> K[PlanResult + execution_metadata]
`} />

`RunDeployV2` is the fail-closed spine: it evaluates the plan JSON with `verify.Evaluate`, refuses
the apply if a hard control is failing and unwaived (`gateRequiresReport` + `Report.Unwaived`), and
seals a `verify.SignedReceipt`. Also exposes `RunDestroy()`, `RunDriftDetection()`, `RunStateImport()`,
and `RunProbe()`. Brownfield attach
is handled here: a component marked "existing" injects the resource id (`vpc_id` / `network_id` /
`vnet_id`) as a tfvar instead of creating one.

records.title: core Library
records.heading: tofu/
records.text:
Drives the `tofu` binary through `hashicorp/terraform-exec/tfexec` (state- and CLI-compatible with
the Terraform 1.6 HCL line, hence the legacy library name):

- `NewTofuCLI()` — construct against a workdir with stage-aware graceful cancellation (SIGINT to the
 `tofu` child on ctx-done, then a grace period)
- `Init()` / `InitWithBackendFile()` — init with backend config (the console HTTP backend file)
- `Plan()` / `PlanRefreshOnly()` — plan, or refresh-only for drift detection
- `Apply()` / `Destroy()` — apply a plan file / destroy
- `ShowPlanJSON()` — the structured plan JSON the UI diff and verify gate consume
- `OverrideTfvarsFromMap()` — materialize a tfvars file from `ProviderTfvars`

The `tofu` binary is **baked into the runner image** (SHA-verified), so no binary is downloaded at
provision time.

records.title: Runner Agent
records.text: Runner Agent. Autonomous execution agent that runs OpenTofu, installs ArgoCD, and streams logs.

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Runner Agent
records.text:
Runner is the execution engine — a single Go binary shipped as a container image. Runners claim
provisioning jobs from the queue, mint per-job cloud credentials keylessly, execute the `tofu`
binary (OpenTofu), install ArgoCD, and stream logs back in real time. The binary is **CLI-free**:
it bundles no `aws`/`gcloud`/`az`, and mints cluster tokens in-process via `runner kube-token` (see
[Cloud Credentials](/runner/cloud-credentials)).

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Key facts
records.text:
Property Value 
 ---------- ------- 
 Language Go (single binary) 
 IaC engine OpenTofu (`tofu`) `v1.9.0`, baked into the image 
 Base image Alpine 3.21, non-root `runner` user 
 Registries GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io/alethialabs-io/runner*`) 
 Versioning release-please (`runner-v*` tags). See [Release System](/concepts/release-system). 
 Job dispatch Push wake stream (SSE `GET /api/runners/wake`) + 30-second safety poll (`POST /api/jobs/claim`) 
 Heartbeat interval 30 seconds (`POST /api/runners/heartbeat`) 
 tofu state Console HTTP state proxy — no object-storage credential on the runner 
 Cloud auth Keyless OIDC per job (no static keys)

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Where a runner runs — the managed fleet vs. self-deployed
records.text:
The word "runtime" splits cleanly into two paths. Do not conflate them.

 Managed fleet Self-deployed (AWS) 
 --- --- --- 
 Operator `managed` `self` / `deployed` 
 Substrate **Hetzner VM warm pool** AWS ECS Fargate (ARM64) 
 Provisioned by the in-app scaler (`apps/console/lib/fleet/`) a `DEPLOY_RUNNER` job running `infra/templates/runner/aws/` 
 Image source GHCR per-cloud image, self-registers via `ALETHIA_RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` GHCR image, registration token injected as an ECS env var 
 Scaling 60s warm-pool loop, sized by queue depth ([Warm-pool scaling](/runner/scale-to-zero)) ECS service `desired_count`, managed by the customer 
 Billing provisioned hours via `runner_usage_sessions` the customer's own AWS bill 

The **managed fleet** is Alethia running runners in the platform account and assuming into the
customer cloud — cheap Hetzner VMs from a GHCR image, sized by an in-app scaler. **ECS Fargate is
not the managed substrate anymore** (the retired AWS ECS + Lambda fleet lived under `infra/fleet-aws`
and is gone). ECS Fargate is real only for a **self-deployed** runner, which a `DEPLOY_RUNNER` job
provisions into the customer's own AWS account from `infra/templates/runner/a

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Operator & provisioning
records.text:
A runner is described by two orthogonal axes: **operator** (`managed` `self`) and, for self
runners, **provisioning** (`deployed` `registered`). This yields three effective categories:

 Category Operator Provisioning Description 
 ---------- ---------- -------------- ------------- 
 **Managed** `managed` — Alethia runs the runner in the platform account (Hetzner VM warm pool) and bills it by provisioned hours. Automatic scaling, no user setup. 
 **Self · Deployed** `self` `deployed` Provisioned into the customer's cloud by an existing runner running `tofu` (Console "Deploy" tab / `alethia runner deploy`). AWS lands on ECS Fargate. 
 **Self · Registered** `self` `registered` Customer brings their own runner — their own IaC or just `alethia runner start` — and registers it for a token. For on-prem or air-gapped environments. 

The legacy `ALETHIA_RUNNER_MODE` (`cloud-hosted`/`self-hosted`) still works as a back-compat
fallback (`cloud-hosted` → `managed`, `self-hosted` → `self`), but `ALETHIA_RUNNER_OPERATOR` is
canonical.

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Picks up jobs
records.text:
A push wake stream (SSE) signals when a job is claimable; the runner calls `POST /api/jobs/claim` on
each wake, with a 30-second safety poll as the fallback if the stream drops. See
[Job Queue Pattern](/concepts/job-queue).

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Claims atomically
records.text: PostgreSQL `claim_next_job()` with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` prevents double-execution.

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Mints credentials
records.text:
Keyless OIDC per job — AWS `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`, GCP Workload Identity Federation, Azure
federated identity, Alibaba `AssumeRoleWithOIDC` — no stored cloud keys. Token clouds
(DigitalOcean / Hetzner / Civo) use an API token, either stored encrypted or kept entirely in a
self-operated runner. See [Cloud Credentials](/runner/cloud-credentials).

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Executes OpenTofu
records.text:
`tofu init` → `tofu plan` → the [verify gate](/runner/job-execution/plan-jobs) → `tofu apply` or
`tofu destroy`. Provisions **greenfield** infrastructure, or **attaches to existing** resources when
the config marks a component "existing" (brownfield — e.g. an existing VPC/VNet). See
[Job Execution](/runner/job-execution).

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Installs ArgoCD
records.text: Helm chart deployment with the App-of-Apps pattern. See [GitOps & ArgoCD](/concepts/gitops-argocd).

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Streams logs
records.text:
Batched POST (notify-driven, flushed on write with a ~1-second backstop) → Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`
→ SSE → browser. See
[Log Streaming](/runner/log-streaming).

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Reports results
records.text:
Updates job status with execution metadata (timing, tofu outputs, and the verify report on
`execution_metadata["verify_result"]`).

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Sends heartbeat
records.text: Every 30 seconds to confirm it is alive.

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Container contents
records.text:
The image builds `FROM` a shared `runner-base` (Alpine 3.21, non-root `runner` user). The base
carries everything cloud-agnostic; each per-cloud image adds only that cloud's project template.

 Tool Purpose 
 ------ --------- 
 Go binary (`runner`) The runner executable — also the `kube-token` exec-credential plugin 
 OpenTofu (`tofu`) `v1.9.0` Infrastructure provisioning (SHA256-verified download, baked in) 
 kubectl Kubernetes cluster access 
 Helm ArgoCD and component installation 
 Infracost `v0.10.39` Cost estimation 
 Infrastructure templates Per-cloud project templates + runner + ArgoCD manifests 
 podman / crun / fuse-overlayfs Nested rootless sandbox runtime — **inert** until `ALETHIA_SANDBOX_BACKEND=container` 

 
 **No cloud CLIs.** The image bundles **no** `aws-cli`, `gcloud`, or `azure-cli` — the
 `Dockerfile`s say so explicitly. EKS/GKE/AKS cluster tokens are minted **in-process** by
 `runner kube-token --provider `, invoked by the exec-credential kubeconfig the runner
 writes. See [Cloud Credentials](/runner/cloud-credentials).

records.title: Runner Agent
records.heading: Documentation
records.text:
Main loop, heartbeat, sandbox seam, graceful shutdown 
 Per-job-type execution details 
 Keyless, per-job credential minting 
 Real-time log delivery 
 In-app scaler + Hetzner VM fleet 
 Running a runner you operate yourself 
 OpenTofu modules for all providers 
 Shared Go packages

records.title: ArgoCD Components
records.text: ArgoCD Components. Pre-installed Kubernetes components managed by ArgoCD after cluster provisioning.

records.title: ArgoCD Components
records.heading: ArgoCD Components
records.text: After cluster provisioning, Runner installs ArgoCD and deploys a set of supporting components via the [App of Apps pattern](/concepts/gitops-argocd). These templates live in `infra/templates/argocd/`.

records.title: ArgoCD Components
records.heading: Component Manifests
records.text:
Template Component Purpose 
 ---------- ----------- --------- 
 `aws-load-balancer-controller.yaml` AWS Load Balancer Controller Provisions ALB/NLB for Kubernetes Ingress and Service resources 
 `external-dns.yaml` External DNS Syncs DNS records from Kubernetes Ingress annotations. Backends: Route53/Cloud DNS/Azure DNS via workload identity, **Hetzner Cloud DNS** via the official webhook sidecar (the connector's Cloud API token; the domain's zone must already exist in Hetzner Cloud DNS), and **Cloudflare** whenever the Cloudflare DNS connector is attached (any cloud). Renders only when DNS is enabled with a domain and the selected backend's identity/token is actually present — otherwise it is skipped rather than deployed broken 
 `external-secrets-operator.yaml` External Secrets Operator Pulls secrets from Secrets Manager/Secret Manager/Key Vault into Kubernetes Secrets. The AWS SecretsManager `ClusterSecretStore` renders on AWS only; the operator itself ships on every cloud 
 `karpenter.yaml` Karpenter Just-in-time node provisioning based on pod resource requests (AWS) 
 `metrics-server.yaml` Metrics Server Provides CPU/memory metrics for the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and `kubectl

records.title: ArgoCD Components
records.heading: How Templates Are Rendered
records.text:
Each template is a Kubernetes manifest with Helm-style placeholders. During deployment, the Runner:

1. Extracts **infrastructure facts** from tofu outputs (cluster name, VPC ID, database endpoints, etc.)
2. Renders the facts into a Helm values file
3. Applies each component manifest as an ArgoCD Application

The ArgoCD Application resources reference Helm charts from public repositories with the infrastructure facts injected as values.

records.title: ArgoCD Components
records.heading: Infrastructure Facts
records.text:
Example facts passed to component Helm charts:

cluster:
 name: api-backend-production
 endpoint: https://ABC123.gr7.eu-west-1.eks.amazonaws.com
 oidcProviderArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:oidc-provider/...

vpc:
 id: vpc-0123456789abcdef0

database:
 endpoint: api-backend-production.cluster-abc123.eu-west-1.rds.amazonaws.com
 port: 5432

cache:
 endpoint: api-backend-production.abc123.euw1.cache.amazonaws.com
 port: 6379

dns:
 domain: api.example.com
 zoneId: Z1234567890

Components use these values for provider-specific configuration (e.g., External DNS needs the hosted zone ID, External Secrets Operator needs the cluster OIDC provider ARN for IRSA).

records.title: ArgoCD Components
records.heading: Adding Custom Applications
records.text: After the initial deployment, users can add their own applications by pushing YAML files to the `manifests/applications/` directory in the infrastructure Git repository. ArgoCD automatically deploys any new Application manifest it discovers.

records.title: AWS Resources
records.heading: Key Features
records.text:
**IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts)** — Kubernetes pods can assume IAM roles via their service account, eliminating the need for static credentials in containers. The EKS module creates an OIDC provider and the IRSA module creates per-service-account IAM roles.

**Karpenter** — Just-in-time node provisioning. Instead of pre-scaling node groups, Karpenter watches for pending pods and launches appropriately-sized EC2 instances within seconds. Supports spot instances and multiple instance families.

**Aurora Serverless v2** — Auto-scaling database with ACU-based capacity (0.5–128 ACUs). Scales to zero-ish (0.5 ACU minimum) during idle periods.

records.heading: Key Features
records.text:
**Azure AD Integration** — AKS integrates with Azure AD for RBAC. Cluster admins are Azure AD users or groups, not separate IAM identities.

**Flexible Server** — Azure's latest managed database tier with zone-redundant HA, automatic backups, and vCore-based scaling (1–64 vCores).

**Cosmos DB** — Globally distributed multi-model database supporting SQL (document), Table (key-value), MongoDB, Cassandra, and Gremlin APIs. Multi-region writes for global distribution.

**Ingress through an Application Gateway** — Azure has no per-Ingress load balancer. Instead, the template provisions one Application Gateway v2, and the Application Gateway Ingress Controller (AGIC) turns every `Ingress` object in the cluster into listeners and routing rules on that gateway. Set `ingressClassName: azure-application-gateway` on your `Ingress` to publish through it. AGIC authenticates with a workload identity, so it holds no static credential.

records.title: Infrastructure Templates Overview
records.text: Infrastructure Templates Overview. OpenTofu modules the runner uses to provision infrastructure across AWS, GCP, Azure, Alibaba, and Hetzner.

records.title: Infrastructure Templates Overview
records.heading: Infrastructure Templates
records.text:
The runner provisions infrastructure using pre-built OpenTofu modules (HCL). These templates are
baked into the runner image at build time — each per-cloud image pre-runs `tofu init` on its
template so no provider/module download happens at job time.

records.title: Infrastructure Templates Overview
records.heading: Template Categories
records.text:
Category Path Purpose 
 ---------- ------ --------- 
 AWS project `infra/templates/project/aws/` User infrastructure on AWS 
 GCP project `infra/templates/project/gcp/` User infrastructure on GCP 
 Azure project `infra/templates/project/azure/` User infrastructure on Azure 
 Alibaba project `infra/templates/project/alibaba/` User infrastructure on Alibaba Cloud

records.title: Infrastructure Templates Overview
records.heading: Template staging (image build)
records.text:
During the [runner release pipeline](/concepts/release-system), templates are `COPY`d into the image
and pre-initialized. The full `runner` image carries all five project templates; each per-cloud image
(`runner-aws`, `runner-hetzner`, …) carries only its own:

infra/templates/project/ → /home/runner/project-templates/ (+ tofu init)
infra/templates/runner/ → /home/runner/runner-templates/
infra/templates/argocd/ → /home/runner/argocd-templates/

records.title: Infrastructure Templates Overview
records.heading: Variable generation
records.text:
When executing a job, the runner materializes a tfvars file from the environment's config snapshot
(`tofu.OverrideTfvarsFromMap`). The provisioner in `packages/core/provisioner/` maps each component
to specific tofu variables (`ProviderTfvars`). See
[Cloud Provider Abstraction](/concepts/cloud-abstraction) for the mapping layer.

records.title: Infrastructure Templates Overview
records.heading: tofu state
records.text:
The runner holds **no object-storage credentials**. State for every template is written through the
**Console HTTP state proxy** — the templates declare `backend "http" {}`, and the runner fetches a
per-job token it exposes as `TF_HTTP_PASSWORD`, so state I/O flows through
`/api/jobs/{id}/state`. See [tofu state](/concepts/terraform-state).

records.title: Build Jobs
records.text: Build Jobs. How the runner executes BUILD jobs — kaniko image builds scheduled in the customer's own cluster, pushed to ECR, reported as a per-service digest map.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Build Jobs
records.text:
`BUILD` jobs turn a project's repo-sourced services into real, pushed container images. For each
service whose source is a repository, the runner schedules a [kaniko](https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/kaniko)
build **inside the customer's own provisioned cluster**, waits for it to finish, captures the pushed
image digest, and reports a per-service digest map. `BUILD` is a first-class job type (`JobType =
"BUILD"`), dispatched to `executeBuild` alongside `PLAN`, `DEPLOY`, and the others.

 
 **Where the build runs.** The customer's Dockerfile executes in **their own cluster**, never on the
 runner. Runner-side work is limited to rendering the Job manifest, running `kubectl` against the
 cluster's API server, and a commit-pinning clone that only fetches data. Because nothing from the
 repository executes on the runner, no BYO sandbox is required for a `BUILD`.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: What gets built
records.text:
The runner builds every service whose `source.kind == "repo"`. Prebuilt-image services
(`source.kind == "image"`) are not buildable and are skipped. If the environment has no repo-sourced
services, the job posts an empty result map and finishes with nothing to do.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Read environment outputs
records.text:
The runner reads the environment's OpenTofu outputs through the per-job
[state proxy](/concepts/terraform-state). Two outputs drive the build:

- `ecr_repository_urls_map` — the per-service registry destination map (service name → repository URL).
- `ecr_build_service_account` — the build identity as `namespace:serviceaccount`.

If `ecr_repository_urls_map` is missing, the job fails: the ECR wiring has not been provisioned, so
there is nowhere to push. Provision the infrastructure before running a `BUILD`. When the
service-account output is absent, the runner falls back to the fixed defaults `alethia-build` /
`kaniko-builder`.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Configure cluster access (keyless)
records.text:
The runner builds an exec-plugin kubeconfig from the already-active federated cloud credentials — the
same CLI-free `runner kube-token` mechanism used by [Deploy Jobs](/runner/job-execution/deploy-jobs).
A `BUILD` needs the cluster, so a kubeconfig failure fails the job.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Ensure the build namespace
records.text:
The runner applies the build namespace (idempotently) so the kaniko Jobs have somewhere to land. The
namespace is labelled `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: alethia`.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Pin the commit
records.text:
For each service, the runner shallow-clones the repository runner-side and resolves `HEAD`, pinning
the exact commit the image is built from. When the repository is private, the job's git token is used
for this clone only — it never reaches the in-cluster Job spec or `execution_metadata`.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Render and apply the kaniko Job
records.text:
The runner renders a kaniko build Job (`imagebuild.RenderBuildJob`) named `build- ` and applies
it. The image is tagged with the resolved commit SHA (immutable and reproducible). Any prior build Job
for the same service is deleted first, so a re-run is idempotent.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Watch to completion
records.text:
The runner polls the Job's conditions until it reports `Complete`, `Failed`, or the per-build deadline
passes. A build has a 30-minute ceiling and is polled every 10 seconds. If the Job fails, the runner
surfaces the last 50 lines of the kaniko log so the Console shows why the Dockerfile build failed.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Capture the digest
records.text:
On success the runner captures the pushed image's digest, in priority order:

1. The build pod's **termination message** — kaniko writes ` @sha256:…` to
 `/dev/termination-log`, so the digest is readable after completion without depending on log retention.
2. The digest line from the kaniko **log** (`sha256:` followed by 64 hex characters).
3. As a loud fallback, the **immutable git-SHA tag** (` : `) — still a pinned reference.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Report results
records.text:
Job status → `PROCESSING`/final with `execution_metadata.build_result`: a map of
`service_name → image_digest_uri`. The Console persists each entry into
`project_services.resolved_image`, so the workload no longer runs a placeholder image.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Fail-closed behavior
records.text:
A `BUILD` never lets the Console treat an unbuilt service as built. The whole job fails when:

- a service has no provisioned ECR destination (infra not provisioned),
- a service's build Job fails, or
- a digest cannot be captured.

Digests captured **before** the failure are still posted — a completed, pushed image is real and
persisting it is idempotent.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: The kaniko build Job
records.text:
The build uses kaniko because it runs rootless, needs no Docker daemon, and pushes to the registry via
the pod ServiceAccount's IRSA. The renderer is pure and deterministic (a fixed service + options
produces the same YAML). Key facts of the rendered Job:

 Field Value 
 --- --- 
 Executor image `gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:v1.23.2` (pinned; overridable) 
 Namespace `alethia-build` (default) 
 Dockerfile the service's `build.dockerfile`, else `Dockerfile` 
 Build context sub-path the service's `build.context`, else its `source.path` 
 Destination tag the resolved commit SHA 
 `backoffLimit` `1` (default) 
 `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` `3600` 
 Resource requests `cpu: 500m`, `memory: 1Gi` 

The kaniko executor image bundles the Amazon ECR credential helper and auto-detects
`*.dkr.ecr.*.amazonaws.com` destinations; IRSA is picked up through the default AWS credential chain
because the container sets `AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG=true`.

When the repository is private, its git token never enters the rendered manifest: it is used only for
the runner-side commit-pinning clone (`resolveHeadSHA`) and is not passed to the in-cluster kaniko
build. No secret material is ever inlined into the rendered

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: Secret boundary
records.text:
Registry credentials never enter `execution_metadata`: the build authenticates in-cluster via IRSA,
the runner holds no registry credential at all, and the digest URI is non-secret. The git token used
for commit pinning stays runner-side and is never written into the Job spec or job metadata.

records.title: Build Jobs
records.heading: See also
records.text:
- [Deploy Jobs](/runner/job-execution/deploy-jobs) — provisions the cluster and the ECR wiring a
 `BUILD` depends on.
- [Cloud Credentials](/runner/cloud-credentials) — the keyless per-job credential minting.
- [OpenTofu state](/concepts/terraform-state) — the per-job state proxy the runner reads outputs from.

records.title: Deploy Jobs
records.text: Deploy Jobs. How the runner executes DEPLOY jobs — the verify gate, tofu apply, keyless kubeconfig, and ArgoCD.

records.title: Deploy Jobs
records.heading: Deploy Jobs
records.text:
`DEPLOY` jobs apply the OpenTofu plan and install ArgoCD on the provisioned cluster. Between the
plan and the apply sits the **fail-closed verify gate** — a real apply will not run while a hard
control is failing.

 
 **Brownfield attach.** A DEPLOY doesn't only create new infrastructure — it can attach to what you
 **already have**. When the environment config marks a component "existing" (e.g. an existing
 VPC/VNet — see [Reuse existing resources](/console/design-project/network#reuse-existing-resources)),
 the runner passes the resource's id into the tofu template instead of creating it, and the template
 `data`-sources the existing resource (and, for networks, resolves its subnets) so the rest of the
 graph wires into it. The provision-vs-existing seam is a `count = var.provision_X ? 1 : 0` guard on
 the create path plus a data source on the existing path. Today this covers networks on AWS/GCP/Azure.

records.title: Deploy Jobs
records.heading: Mint cloud credentials
records.text: Same keyless per-job minting as PLAN jobs. See [Cloud Credentials](/runner/cloud-credentials).

records.title: Deploy Jobs
records.heading: Download plan artifact
records.text:
Fetches the binary `plan.tfplan` from the PLAN job (`GET /api/jobs/{planJobId}/plan-artifact`) into
the job workdir. If it can't be fetched, the runner re-plans.

records.title: Deploy Jobs
records.heading: Validate config hash
records.text:
Compares the environment's current `configuration_hash` against the plan job's. If they differ (the
project was edited after planning), the job fails:

> "configuration changed since plan was generated"

This prevents applying a stale plan. See [Plan & Apply](/console/jobs/plan-and-apply).

records.title: Deploy Jobs
